<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Fix booking funnel gaps">
Fix four live-UAT findings in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm (public booking funnel). You own: lib/cleaner_crm/booking.ex (EXCEPT confirm_booking/submit_payment — another agent takes those next; don't touch them), lib/cleaner_crm/booking/lead.ex, lib/cleaner_crm/quoting* (rate card), lib/cleaner_crm/accounts* (one additive flag), lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/booking_live/quote.ex, lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/settings_live/booking_policy.ex, lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/quote_live/rate_card.ex, + migrations (timestamp prefix 202607092000xx) + tests. Do NOT touch the running UAT deploy, kamal, or dev _build.

MCP note: on "No session_id available" add session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8"; if MCP hangs >2 min, message me and keep coding.

CONTEXT: routes now live under /app (e.g. /app/settings/booking, /app/quotes/rate-card); /book is public. Read the current router first.

1. STOREFRONT ACCOUNT (the big one — live regression): Booking.public_scope resolves the NEWEST account (resolve_public_account_id order_by inserted_at desc). Any new signup creating a company silently steals the public /book storefront — happened on UAT (3 accounts named "Desert First Cleaning"; newest has a blank rate card → every combination shows the custom-quote fallback). Fix: add a `storefront` boolean (default false) to accounts (migration + schema, additive only). public_scope resolves: the account with storefront=true; if none, an account only when EXACTLY ONE exists; else nil (BookingLive.Quote already renders the unavailable state for nil — verify it still does). Owner UI: a toggle on /app/settings/booking ("Use this company as the public booking storefront") — setting it true unsets any other account's flag in one transaction (Accounts context function, e.g. Accounts.set_storefront/2, owner-role-gated by the page it lives on).
2. QUOTE INPUT BOUNDS: Lead + the calculator changeset currently accept any integers. Enforce: bedroom_count 0..20, bathroom_count 0..20, square_feet 200..20000 (message like "between 200 and 20,000 sq ft"), hours 1..12 ("between 1 and 12 hours"). Same bounds in the calculator preview changeset so errors show live.
3. MINIMUM VISIT PRICE: add `minimum_visit_cents` to the rate card (migration; editable as dollars on /app/quotes/rate-card with the other fields; default nil = no floor). Quoting/Booking quote_summary clamps: total = max(computed, minimum) when minimum set, and expose a flag so the calculator can show "Includes our minimum visit price." — kills the 1-sqft $0.12 quote class even before input bounds.
4. EMAIL FORMAT on leads: validate client_email format (reuse the same regex/approach Users.User uses for email). NOTE: true verification (click-a-link-before-booking) is a product decision we are NOT making here — format-only.

Existing specs to keep green: full PORT=4002 mix spex (143 — 848/849 drive this funnel; if a spec used out-of-bounds fixture values, adjust the FIXTURE VALUES to valid ones, never weaken app validation) + full PORT=4002 MIX_ENV=test mix test (266+, kill port 4002 first) + compile --warnings-as-errors + mix format. Add regression tests for each fix (storefront resolution incl. the two-account-no-flag → nil case; bounds; floor; email).

Final response: what changed per fix, migration names, test counts, "NEEDS RELEASE REBUILD + MIGRATE". Under 180 words.
</teammate-message>

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authenticated app surface

  # Every LiveView under /app/* is the "app" chrome (drawer + sidebar shell
  # via Layouts.app). The /app prefix is the source of truth that
  # distinguishes the app layout from the public/portal layouts (`/`,
  # `/book`, `/portal`, ...).
  scope "/app", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    # Authenticated, no account required. Account management lives here
    # (not gated by RequireAccount) so a user with no company yet can
    # still reach account creation instead of being locked out of the
    # one page that lets them create one.
    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index
    end

    # Field surfaces need an active account: every scoped query guards
    # on `active_account_id`, so a freshly-registered user with no
    # company is funneled to /app/accounts/new instead of crashing.
    live_session :require_account,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default}
      ] do
      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reviews, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/app/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above. RequireAccount runs
    # first so an account-less user goes to company creation, not into
    # RequireOfficeRole's /app/field redirect (which would also crash).
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/rate-card", QuoteLive.RateCard, :edit
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index

      live "/reviews", ReviewLive.Index, :index

      live "/settings/booking", SettingsLive.BookingPolicy, :edit
    end
  end

  # Office-only controller route (the payroll CSV export) — layered on
  # `:require_office_role` since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  scope "/app", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  # Authenticated routes that must stay at the root path (not under
  # /app): the password-update form posts here, and the OAuth
  # connect/callback URLs are registered with the external provider
  # (CodeMySpec's redirect URI), so they can't move.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password

    scope "/integrations/oauth" do
      get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
      get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
    end
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end

  # Reviews (story 853): the public token-link review page needs no
  # login — mirrors `/invitations/accept/:token`'s `:current_user`
  # live_session so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout.
  # No collision with the office inbox at `/app/reviews` — that lives
  # under the `/app` scope above.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :reviews_public,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/reviews/:token", ReviewLive.Public, :show
    end
  end

  # Portal (client magic-link) — no user auth. `/portal/access/:token`
  # exchanges a mailed/booking-issued token for a portal session
  # (plain `:browser`, like the reminder confirm/reschedule links
  # above, so `fetch_session`/`fetch_current_scope_for_user` still
  # run); every other portal route sits behind
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth`'s own session check instead.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    get "/portal/access/:token", PortalController, :access

    live_session :portal,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
      live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      live "/portal/visits/:id", PortalLive.Visit, :show
      live "/portal/invoices", PortalLive.Invoices, :index
    end
  end

  # Public booking funnel (stories 848/849) — no user auth, plain
  # `:browser` (like the reminder/reviews/portal public routes above)
  # so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout. Both routes
  # share one view module, `BookingLive.Quote` — see its moduledoc for
  # why `BookingLive.Accept` isn't routed on its own.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :public_booking,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/book", BookingLive.Quote, :new
      live "/book/accept/:token", BookingLive.Quote, :accept
    end
  end
end

    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authenticated app surface

  # Every LiveView under /app/* is the "app" chrome (drawer + sidebar shell
  # via Layouts.app). The /app prefix is the source of truth that
  # distinguishes the app layout from the public/portal layouts (`/`,
  # `/book`, `/portal`, ...).
  scope "/app", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    # Authenticated, no account required. Account management lives here
    # (not gated by RequireAccount) so a user with no company yet can
    # still reach account creation instead of being locked out of the
    # one page that lets them create one.
    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index
    end

    # Field surfaces need an active account: every scoped query guards
    # on `active_account_id`, so a freshly-registered user with no
    # company is funneled to /app/accounts/new instead of crashing.
    live_session :require_account,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default}
      ] do
      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reviews, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/app/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above. RequireAccount runs
    # first so an account-less user goes to company creation, not into
    # RequireOfficeRole's /app/field redirect (which would also crash).
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/rate-card", QuoteLive.RateCard, :edit
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index

      live "/reviews", ReviewLive.Index, :index

      live "/settings/booking", SettingsLive.BookingPolicy, :edit
    end
  end

  # Office-only controller route (the payroll CSV export) — layered on
  # `:require_office_role` since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  scope "/app", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  # Authenticated routes that must stay at the root path (not under
  # /app): the password-update form posts here, and the OAuth
  # connect/callback URLs are registered with the external provider
  # (CodeMySpec's redirect URI), so they can't move.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password

    scope "/integrations/oauth" do
      get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
      get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
    end
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end

  # Reviews (story 853): the public token-link review page needs no
  # login — mirrors `/invitations/accept/:token`'s `:current_user`
  # live_session so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout.
  # No collision with the office inbox at `/app/reviews` — that lives
  # under the `/app` scope above.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :reviews_public,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/reviews/:token", ReviewLive.Public, :show
    end
  end

  # Portal (client magic-link) — no user auth. `/portal/access/:token`
  # exchanges a mailed/booking-issued token for a portal session
  # (plain `:browser`, like the reminder confirm/reschedule links
  # above, so `fetch_session`/`fetch_current_scope_for_user` still
  # run); every other portal route sits behind
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth`'s own session check instead.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    get "/portal/access/:token", PortalController, :access

    live_session :portal,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
      live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      live "/portal/visits/:id", PortalLive.Visit, :show
      live "/portal/invoices", PortalLive.Invoices, :index
    end
  end

  # Public booking funnel (stories 848/849) — no user auth, plain
  # `:browser` (like the reminder/reviews/portal public routes above)
  # so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout. Both routes
  # share one view module, `BookingLive.Quote` — see its moduledoc for
  # why `BookingLive.Accept` isn't routed on its own.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :public_booking,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/book", BookingLive.Quote, :new
      live "/book/accept/:token", BookingLive.Quote, :accept
    end
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Public acquisition funnel (stories 848/849): the instant-quote
4	  calculator, capturing a lead's contact info once a price is shown,
5	  and quote acceptance — slot selection, cancellation-policy
6	  agreement, and Stripe card capture — that converts an accepted lead
7	  into a client + property + plan/job and issues portal access.
8	
9	  Orchestrates `CleanerCrm.Quoting` (rate-card pricing, via
10	  `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`), `CleanerCrm.Clients` (client +
11	  property), `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` (job/plan + slot availability),
12	  `CleanerCrm.Billing` (card capture via its `StripeGateway`), and
13	  `CleanerCrm.Portal` (the confirmation's magic-link).
14	
15	  Every function here is either scoped by an explicit `Scope`
16	  (mirroring every other context) or takes a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead`
17	  directly and resolves its own account scope from it — none of them
18	  are reachable from a logged-in user, so there's no caller `Scope` to
19	  receive from a plug.
20	
21	  ## Single-tenant storefront (known MVP limitation)
22	
23	  `/book` carries no account identifier — no slug, no subdomain — so
24	  `public_scope/0` resolves to the *most recently created* account
25	  rather than *the right* one, matching the single-account assumption
26	  every story-848 spec drives (each spec's own account is the newest
27	  one the moment it hits `/book`, so this holds even alongside stray
28	  older rows). A multi-tenant deployment needs its own story to give
29	  each business a distinct public booking URL (e.g. `/book/:slug`)
30	  before this holds up outside a single-account deployment or test.
31	  """
32	
33	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
34	
35	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account
36	  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway
37	  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.{Lead, Notifier, Pricing}
38	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
39	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
40	  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
41	  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
42	  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard
43	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
44	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
45	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
46	
47	  # A reasonable number of visits to materialize up front for a
48	  # recurring booking, matching the office's own recurring-plan
49	  # builder default order of magnitude (see
50	  # `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent`) — the office can
51	  # always add more from the schedule board afterward.
52	  @default_occurrence_count 12
53	  @default_visit_duration_seconds 2 * 60 * 60
54	
55	  ## Public storefront
56	
57	  @doc "The (single-account MVP) scope every unauthenticated booking-funnel call resolves against."
58	  def public_scope, do: %Scope{active_account_id: resolve_public_account_id()}
59	
60	  @doc "The public rate card the instant-quote calculator prices against."
61	  def get_rate_card(%Scope{} = scope), do: Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)
62	
63	  defp resolve_public_account_id do
64	    Account
65	    |> order_by(desc: :inserted_at)
66	    |> limit(1)
67	    |> select([a], a.id)
68	    |> Repo.one()
69	  end
70	
71	  ## Instant quote (calculator)
72	
73	  @doc """
74	  The calculator's live-preview changeset — never persisted, so the
75	  price can be computed before any contact info exists (see
76	  `quote_summary/2`).
77	  """
78	  def change_lead(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.quote_changeset(lead, attrs)
79	
80	  @doc "Everything `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` needs to render the live total."
81	  def quote_summary(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead),
82	    do: Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)
83	
84	  @doc """
85	  Captures a visitor's contact info against their computed price —
86	  locking in the quote as an accepted lead with its own acceptance
87	  token, the moment `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote`'s contact form is
88	  submitted. Always saved as `:accepted`: a lead is only ever persisted
89	  once contact info makes it one.
90	  """
91	  def create_lead(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
92	    %Lead{account_id: account_id}
93	    |> Lead.changeset(Map.merge(attrs, %{acceptance_token: generate_token(), status: :accepted}))
94	    |> Repo.insert()
95	  end
96	
97	  @doc "Looks up an accepted lead by its public acceptance-link token. No `Scope` — the token is the access control."
98	  def get_lead_by_token(token) when is_binary(token),
99	    do: Repo.get_by(Lead, acceptance_token: token)
100	
101	  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)
102	
103	  ## Acceptance: slot selection
104	
105	  def change_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.slot_changeset(lead, attrs)
106	
107	  @doc """
108	  Validates and applies a slot choice to the (still unpersisted) lead
109	  — rejected outright if the chosen date/time is already in the past
110	  (see `Lead.slot_changeset/3`). Nothing reaches the database here —
111	  `confirm_booking/3` is the only place a slot gets written, so
112	  availability (and, per issue 4e985412, whether the slot is still in
113	  the future) is always checked again right before a card is ever
114	  charged, no matter how long a client lingers on the
115	  cancellation-policy step. `now` defaults to the real clock but takes
116	  an override for tests.
117	  """
118	  def select_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
119	    with {:ok, %Lead{start_time: start_time} = slotted} <-
120	           lead |> Lead.slot_changeset(attrs, now) |> Ecto.Changeset.apply_action(:update) do
121	      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
122	    end
123	  end
124	
125	  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
126	    candidate = Time.add(start_time, @default_visit_duration_seconds, :second)
127	    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
128	  end
129	
130	  ## Acceptance: cancellation policy + payment
131	
132	  def change_confirmation(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}),
133	    do: Lead.confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs)
134	
135	  @doc "Whether the lead's selected slot is still free, account-wide (single-crew capacity, not per-cleaner)."
136	  def slot_available?(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: false
137	
138	  def slot_available?(%Lead{} = lead) do
139	    Scheduling.slot_available?(
140	      scope_for(lead),
141	      lead.scheduled_date,
142	      lead.start_time,
143	      lead.end_time
144	    )
145	  end
146	
147	  @doc """
148	  The confirmation step. Refuses without charging anything when the
149	  cancellation policy isn't agreed to, the selected slot has already
150	  passed, or the slot's been claimed by another booking since it was
151	  selected — otherwise submits the card and moves the lead to
152	  `:payment_pending`. Only the Stripe webhook
153	  (`receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever confirms or declines it from
154	  there, per the same webhook-confirms-everything rule
155	  `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for invoice payments.
156	
157	  The past-slot check (issue 4e985412) is defense in depth alongside
158	  `Lead.slot_changeset/3`'s own form-level validation: a slot picked
159	  as "later today" can go stale by the time the client actually
160	  submits payment, the same reason `slot_available?/1` is re-checked
161	  here rather than trusted from selection time. `now` defaults to the
162	  real clock but takes an override for tests.
163	  """
164	  def confirm_booking(lead, params, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())
165	
166	  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, %{"payment_method" => payment_method} = params, now) do
167	    cond do
168	      Map.get(params, "policy_agreed") not in [true, "true"] ->
169	        {:error, :policy_required}
170	
171	      not Lead.slot_in_future?(lead, now) ->
172	        {:error, :slot_in_past}
173	
174	      not slot_available?(lead) ->
175	        {:error, :slot_unavailable}
176	
177	      true ->
178	        submit_payment(lead, payment_method)
179	    end
180	  end
181	
182	  defp submit_payment(%Lead{} = lead, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
183	    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
184	           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
185	             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
186	             payment_method: payment_method,
187	             off_session: false,
188	             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
189	           }) do
190	      lead
191	      |> Lead.changeset(%{

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking do
  @moduledoc """
  Public acquisition funnel (stories 848/849): the instant-quote
  calculator, capturing a lead's contact info once a price is shown,
  and quote acceptance — slot selection, cancellation-policy
  agreement, and Stripe card capture — that converts an accepted lead
  into a client + property + plan/job and issues portal access.

  Orchestrates `CleanerCrm.Quoting` (rate-card pricing, via
  `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`), `CleanerCrm.Clients` (client +
  property), `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` (job/plan + slot availability),
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` (card capture via its `StripeGateway`), and
  `CleanerCrm.Portal` (the confirmation's magic-link).

  Every function here is either scoped by an explicit `Scope`
  (mirroring every other context) or takes a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead`
  directly and resolves its own account scope from it — none of them
  are reachable from a logged-in user, so there's no caller `Scope` to
  receive from a plug.

  ## Single-tenant storefront (known MVP limitation)

  `/book` carries no account identifier — no slug, no subdomain — so
  `public_scope/0` resolves to the *most recently created* account
  rather than *the right* one, matching the single-account assumption
  every story-848 spec drives (each spec's own account is the newest
  one the moment it hits `/book`, so this holds even alongside stray
  older rows). A multi-tenant deployment needs its own story to give
  each business a distinct public booking URL (e.g. `/book/:slug`)
  before this holds up outside a single-account deployment or test.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account
  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.{Lead, Notifier, Pricing}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # A reasonable number of visits to materialize up front for a
  # recurring booking, matching the office's own recurring-plan
  # builder default order of magnitude (see
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.PlanFormComponent`) — the office can
  # always add more from the schedule board afterward.
  @default_occurrence_count 12
  @default_visit_duration_seconds 2 * 60 * 60

  ## Public storefront

  @doc "The (single-account MVP) scope every unauthenticated booking-funnel call resolves against."
  def public_scope, do: %Scope{active_account_id: resolve_public_account_id()}

  @doc "The public rate card the instant-quote calculator prices against."
  def get_rate_card(%Scope{} = scope), do: Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)

  defp resolve_public_account_id do
    Account
    |> order_by(desc: :inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([a], a.id)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Instant quote (calculator)

  @doc """
  The calculator's live-preview changeset — never persisted, so the
  price can be computed before any contact info exists (see
  `quote_summary/2`).
  """
  def change_lead(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.quote_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc "Everything `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` needs to render the live total."
  def quote_summary(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead),
    do: Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)

  @doc """
  Captures a visitor's contact info against their computed price —
  locking in the quote as an accepted lead with its own acceptance
  token, the moment `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote`'s contact form is
  submitted. Always saved as `:accepted`: a lead is only ever persisted
  once contact info makes it one.
  """
  def create_lead(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Lead{account_id: account_id}
    |> Lead.changeset(Map.merge(attrs, %{acceptance_token: generate_token(), status: :accepted}))
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "Looks up an accepted lead by its public acceptance-link token. No `Scope` — the token is the access control."
  def get_lead_by_token(token) when is_binary(token),
    do: Repo.get_by(Lead, acceptance_token: token)

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  ## Acceptance: slot selection

  def change_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}), do: Lead.slot_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc """
  Validates and applies a slot choice to the (still unpersisted) lead
  — rejected outright if the chosen date/time is already in the past
  (see `Lead.slot_changeset/3`). Nothing reaches the database here —
  `confirm_booking/3` is the only place a slot gets written, so
  availability (and, per issue 4e985412, whether the slot is still in
  the future) is always checked again right before a card is ever
  charged, no matter how long a client lingers on the
  cancellation-policy step. `now` defaults to the real clock but takes
  an override for tests.
  """
  def select_slot(%Lead{} = lead, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    with {:ok, %Lead{start_time: start_time} = slotted} <-
           lead |> Lead.slot_changeset(attrs, now) |> Ecto.Changeset.apply_action(:update) do
      {:ok, %{slotted | end_time: default_end_time(start_time)}}
    end
  end

  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, @default_visit_duration_seconds, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  ## Acceptance: cancellation policy + payment

  def change_confirmation(%Lead{} = lead, attrs \\ %{}),
    do: Lead.confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs)

  @doc "Whether the lead's selected slot is still free, account-wide (single-crew capacity, not per-cleaner)."
  def slot_available?(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: false

  def slot_available?(%Lead{} = lead) do
    Scheduling.slot_available?(
      scope_for(lead),
      lead.scheduled_date,
      lead.start_time,
      lead.end_time
    )
  end

  @doc """
  The confirmation step. Refuses without charging anything when the
  cancellation policy isn't agreed to, the selected slot has already
  passed, or the slot's been claimed by another booking since it was
  selected — otherwise submits the card and moves the lead to
  `:payment_pending`. Only the Stripe webhook
  (`receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever confirms or declines it from
  there, per the same webhook-confirms-everything rule
  `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for invoice payments.

  The past-slot check (issue 4e985412) is defense in depth alongside
  `Lead.slot_changeset/3`'s own form-level validation: a slot picked
  as "later today" can go stale by the time the client actually
  submits payment, the same reason `slot_available?/1` is re-checked
  here rather than trusted from selection time. `now` defaults to the
  real clock but takes an override for tests.
  """
  def confirm_booking(lead, params, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())

  def confirm_booking(%Lead{} = lead, %{"payment_method" => payment_method} = params, now) do
    cond do
      Map.get(params, "policy_agreed") not in [true, "true"] ->
        {:error, :policy_required}

      not Lead.slot_in_future?(lead, now) ->
        {:error, :slot_in_past}

      not slot_available?(lead) ->
        {:error, :slot_unavailable}

      true ->
        submit_payment(lead, payment_method)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(%Lead{} = lead, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
             amount_cents: lead.total_cents,
             payment_method: payment_method,
             off_session: false,
             metadata: %{lead_id: lead.id}
           }) do
      lead
      |> Lead.changeset(%{
        policy_agreed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
        status: :payment_pending,
        stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id
      })
      # `select_slot/2` never touches the database (see its doc) — the
      # slot lives only on this in-memory `lead` struct until now, so
      # `cast/3` (which diffs against the struct's own field, not the
      # row) would otherwise see "no change" and silently leave the
      # database's scheduled_date/start_time/end_time at `nil`.
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:scheduled_date, lead.scheduled_date)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:start_time, lead.start_time)
      |> Ecto.Changeset.force_change(:end_time, lead.end_time)
      |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request for a
  booking's payment — `CleanerCrmWeb.StripeWebhookController` falls
  back to this once `CleanerCrm.Billing.receive_webhook/1` reports the
  event isn't one of its own invoices.
  """
  def receive_payment_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      convert_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, lead} <- find_lead_for_event(event) do
      decline_lead(lead)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:error, :lead_not_found}

  defp find_lead_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"lead_id" => lead_id}} when is_binary(lead_id) -> fetch_lead(lead_id)
      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) -> fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id)
      _ -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead(lead_id) do
    case Repo.get(Lead, lead_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_lead_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Lead, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :lead_not_found}
      lead -> {:ok, lead}
    end
  end

  defp decline_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    lead |> Lead.changeset(%{status: :payment_declined}) |> Repo.update()
  end

  # Idempotent against a redelivered webhook — Stripe (and its Test
  # stand-in) offers no stronger delivery guarantee than at-least-once.
  defp convert_lead(%Lead{status: :converted} = lead), do: {:ok, lead}

  defp convert_lead(%Lead{} = lead) do
    scope = scope_for(lead)

    with {:ok, {updated, client}} <-
           Repo.transact(fn ->
             with {:ok, client} <- Clients.create_client(scope, client_attrs(lead)),
                  {:ok, property} <- Clients.create_property(scope, property_attrs(client)),
                  {:ok, visit_ids} <- schedule_visit(scope, lead, property),
                  {:ok, updated} <- finalize_conversion(lead, client, property, visit_ids) do
               {:ok, {updated, client}}
             end
           end) do
      issue_portal_access(updated, client)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp client_attrs(%Lead{} = lead) do
    %{
      name: lead.client_name,
      email: lead.client_email,
      phone: lead.client_phone,
      card_on_file: true
    }
  end

  # No property inputs exist anywhere in the public funnel (story 848's
  # form only ever asks for what prices the job) — the office fills
  # the real address in from the client record afterward. Named after
  # the client rather than a generic placeholder so the schedule board
  # (which shows a job's property, never its client, on the card) still
  # identifies whose visit this is until that happens.
  defp property_attrs(%Client{} = client) do
    %{client_id: client.id, service_address: "#{client.name} — address to be confirmed"}
  end

  defp schedule_visit(scope, %Lead{frequency: :one_time} = lead, property) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           Scheduling.create_job(scope, %{
             property_id: property.id,
             scheduled_date: lead.scheduled_date,
             start_time: lead.start_time,
             end_time: lead.end_time,
             agreed_price_cents: lead.total_cents,
             status: :scheduled
           }) do
      {:ok, %{job_id: job.id, recurring_plan_id: nil}}
    end
  end

  defp schedule_visit(scope, %Lead{} = lead, property) do
    with {:ok, {plan, _jobs}} <-
           Scheduling.create_recurring_plan(scope, %{
             property_id: property.id,
             recurrence: lead.frequency,
             start_date: lead.scheduled_date,
             occurrence_count: @default_occurrence_count,
             start_time: lead.start_time,
             end_time: lead.end_time,
             agreed_price_cents: lead.total_cents
           }) do
      {:ok, %{job_id: nil, recurring_plan_id: plan.id}}
    end
  end

  defp finalize_conversion(%Lead{} = lead, %Client{} = client, property, visit_ids) do
    lead
    |> Lead.changeset(
      Map.merge(%{status: :converted, client_id: client.id, property_id: property.id}, visit_ids)
    )
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp issue_portal_access(%Lead{} = lead, %Client{} = client) do
    with {:ok, session} <- Portal.create_portal_session(client, %{}) do
      Notifier.deliver_confirmation(lead, portal_url(session))
    end
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp portal_url(session), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/portal/access/#{session.token}"

  defp scope_for(%Lead{account_id: account_id}), do: %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}
end

2	  @moduledoc """
3	  A public instant-quote submission (story 848/849): the property
4	  inputs and frequency/add-ons it was priced from, the price snapshot
5	  frozen at the moment contact info was captured, the client's contact
6	  details, and everything the acceptance flow (slot, cancellation-policy
7	  agreement, card) adds on top of it.
8	
9	  ## Status
10	
11	  `:quoted` — never actually persisted today (the calculator on `/book`
12	  prices a lead purely in memory, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.change_lead/2`)
13	  but kept as the schema default for a row that, in principle, exists
14	  before contact info locks it in.
15	
16	  `:accepted` -> `:payment_pending` -> `:converted`, or `:payment_pending`
17	  -> `:payment_declined` (from which the client can retry). Only a
18	  Stripe webhook (`CleanerCrm.Booking.receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever
19	  moves a lead into `:converted` or `:payment_declined` — submitting
20	  the card just moves it to `:payment_pending`, per the same
21	  webhook-confirms-everything rule `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for
22	  invoice payments.
23	  """
24	
25	  use Ecto.Schema
26	  import Ecto.Changeset
27	
28	  @type pricing_model :: :per_room | :per_sqft | :hourly
29	  @type frequency :: :one_time | :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly
30	  @type status :: :quoted | :accepted | :payment_pending | :payment_declined | :converted
31	
32	  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
33	          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
34	          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
35	          pricing_model: pricing_model() | nil,
36	          bedroom_count: integer() | nil,
37	          bathroom_count: integer() | nil,
38	          square_feet: integer() | nil,
39	          hours: integer() | nil,
40	          frequency: frequency(),
41	          add_ons: [String.t()],
42	          total_cents: integer() | nil,
43	          status: status(),
44	          client_name: String.t() | nil,
45	          client_email: String.t() | nil,
46	          client_phone: String.t() | nil,
47	          acceptance_token: String.t() | nil,
48	          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
49	          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
50	          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
51	          policy_agreed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
52	          policy_agreed: boolean() | nil,
53	          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
54	          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
55	          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
56	          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
57	          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
58	          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
59	          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
60	        }
61	
62	  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
63	  schema "leads" do
64	    field :pricing_model, Ecto.Enum, values: [:per_room, :per_sqft, :hourly]
65	    field :bedroom_count, :integer
66	    field :bathroom_count, :integer
67	    field :square_feet, :integer
68	    field :hours, :integer
69	
70	    field :frequency, Ecto.Enum,
71	      values: [:one_time, :weekly, :biweekly, :monthly],
72	      default: :one_time
73	
74	    field :add_ons, {:array, :string}, default: []
75	    field :total_cents, :integer
76	
77	    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
78	      values: [:quoted, :accepted, :payment_pending, :payment_declined, :converted],

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead do
  @moduledoc """
  A public instant-quote submission (story 848/849): the property
  inputs and frequency/add-ons it was priced from, the price snapshot
  frozen at the moment contact info was captured, the client's contact
  details, and everything the acceptance flow (slot, cancellation-policy
  agreement, card) adds on top of it.

  ## Status

  `:quoted` — never actually persisted today (the calculator on `/book`
  prices a lead purely in memory, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.change_lead/2`)
  but kept as the schema default for a row that, in principle, exists
  before contact info locks it in.

  `:accepted` -> `:payment_pending` -> `:converted`, or `:payment_pending`
  -> `:payment_declined` (from which the client can retry). Only a
  Stripe webhook (`CleanerCrm.Booking.receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever
  moves a lead into `:converted` or `:payment_declined` — submitting
  the card just moves it to `:payment_pending`, per the same
  webhook-confirms-everything rule `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for
  invoice payments.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type pricing_model :: :per_room | :per_sqft | :hourly
  @type frequency :: :one_time | :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly
  @type status :: :quoted | :accepted | :payment_pending | :payment_declined | :converted

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          pricing_model: pricing_model() | nil,
          bedroom_count: integer() | nil,
          bathroom_count: integer() | nil,
          square_feet: integer() | nil,
          hours: integer() | nil,
          frequency: frequency(),
          add_ons: [String.t()],
          total_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          client_name: String.t() | nil,
          client_email: String.t() | nil,
          client_phone: String.t() | nil,
          acceptance_token: String.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          policy_agreed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          policy_agreed: boolean() | nil,
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "leads" do
    field :pricing_model, Ecto.Enum, values: [:per_room, :per_sqft, :hourly]
    field :bedroom_count, :integer
    field :bathroom_count, :integer
    field :square_feet, :integer
    field :hours, :integer

    field :frequency, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:one_time, :weekly, :biweekly, :monthly],
      default: :one_time

    field :add_ons, {:array, :string}, default: []
    field :total_cents, :integer

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:quoted, :accepted, :payment_pending, :payment_declined, :converted],
      default: :quoted

    field :client_name, :string
    field :client_email, :string
    field :client_phone, :string

    field :acceptance_token, :string

    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time
    field :policy_agreed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    # Not persisted as a boolean column — `confirm_booking/2` turns a
    # truthy submission into `policy_agreed_at` instead. Only exists so
    # the confirmation form has a real changeset field to bind its
    # agreement checkbox to.
    field :policy_agreed, :boolean, virtual: true, default: false

    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @quote_fields ~w(pricing_model bedroom_count bathroom_count square_feet hours frequency add_ons)a

  @doc """
  The calculator's own changeset — every pricing input, none of it
  required, so `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing` can price a live preview
  (via `Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes/1`) after every keystroke
  regardless of whether the changeset is complete yet.
  """
  def quote_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> cast(normalize_add_ons(attrs), @quote_fields)
    |> validate_number(:bedroom_count, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:bathroom_count, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:square_feet, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:hours, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
  end

  @doc """
  The full changeset used once a lead is actually persisted: the
  calculator's inputs plus the price snapshot, contact details, and
  every field the acceptance flow fills in afterward.
  """
  def changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> quote_changeset(attrs)
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :total_cents,
      :status,
      :client_name,
      :client_email,
      :client_phone,
      :acceptance_token,
      :scheduled_date,
      :start_time,
      :end_time,
      :policy_agreed_at,
      :stripe_payment_intent_id,
      :client_id,
      :property_id,
      :job_id,
      :recurring_plan_id
    ])
    |> validate_required([:client_name, :client_email, :client_phone], message: "is required")
    |> validate_number(:total_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:acceptance_token)
  end

  @doc """
  The slot-selection step's own changeset — the chosen date and start
  time, required and rejected outright if already in the past (issue
  4e985412: this form accepted any date, including years-old ones,
  with zero validation). `now` defaults to the real clock but takes an
  override so callers can test the boundary without sleeping.
  """
  def slot_changeset(lead, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    lead
    |> cast(attrs, [:scheduled_date, :start_time])
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time], message: "is required")
    |> validate_slot_in_future(now)
  end

  @doc "The confirmation step's own changeset — the policy-agreement checkbox."
  def confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    cast(lead, attrs, [:policy_agreed])
  end

  @doc """
  Whether a lead's `scheduled_date`/`start_time` are still ahead of
  `now` (defaulting to the real clock) — today counts only if
  `start_time` hasn't passed yet. `false` for either field unset.

  The single source of truth behind two checks: `slot_changeset/3`'s
  own validation above (the form-level guard), and
  `CleanerCrm.Booking.confirm_booking/3`'s defense-in-depth re-check
  right before a card is charged — a slot picked as "later today" can
  go stale by the time the client actually submits payment, the same
  reason `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.slot_available?/4` gets re-checked
  there too.
  """
  @spec slot_in_future?(t(), DateTime.t()) :: boolean()
  def slot_in_future?(lead, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())

  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: nil}, _now), do: false
  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{start_time: nil}, _now), do: false

  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: date, start_time: start_time}, now) do
    case Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) do
      :gt -> true
      :lt -> false
      :eq -> Time.compare(start_time, DateTime.to_time(now)) == :gt
    end
  end

  defp validate_slot_in_future(changeset, now) do
    date = get_field(changeset, :scheduled_date)
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)

    cond do
      is_nil(date) or is_nil(start_time) ->
        changeset

      slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: date, start_time: start_time}, now) ->
        changeset

      Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) == :lt ->
        add_error(changeset, :scheduled_date, "must be today or later")

      true ->
        add_error(changeset, :start_time, "must be later than the current time")
    end
  end

  # A hidden fallback input keeps `quote[add_ons][]` present in the
  # form even with every add-on unchecked (so unchecking the last one
  # actually clears it) at the cost of always submitting one blank
  # entry alongside any real ones — dropped here rather than left for
  # every caller to filter.
  defp normalize_add_ons(%{"add_ons" => list} = attrs) when is_list(list),
    do: %{attrs | "add_ons" => Enum.reject(list, &(&1 in [nil, ""]))}

  defp normalize_add_ons(attrs), do: attrs
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting do
  @moduledoc """
  Quotes built from the account's rate card using per-room, per-sqft,
  or hourly pricing models.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. A quote is
  built up in memory (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`) and only ever
  persisted at the moment it's sent — `send_quote/3` freezes the rate
  card's current rates into the quote's line items, so later rate-card
  edits never alter an already-sent quote.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, QuoteItem, RateCard, Pricing}

  ## Rate card

  @doc """
  Returns the account's rate card, creating a blank one on first use.
  """
  def get_or_create_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(RateCard, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> Repo.insert!(%RateCard{account_id: account_id})
      rate_card -> rate_card
    end
  end

  def change_rate_card(%Scope{}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RateCard.changeset(rate_card, attrs)
  end

  def update_rate_card(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %RateCard{} = rate_card, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    rate_card
    |> RateCard.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  ## Quotes

  def change_quote(%Scope{}, %Quote{} = quote, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Quote.changeset(quote, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists the account's quotes, most recently sent first.
  """
  def list_quotes(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Quote
    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([q], desc: q.inserted_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_quote!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Quote
    |> where([q], q.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(:quote_items)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Finalizes a draft quote against the current rate card: prices every
  line item, then inserts the quote and its `CleanerCrm.Quoting.QuoteItem`s
  together, freezing the rates and amounts at this moment.

  Refuses with `{:error, :not_finalizable}` when any priced line item
  is missing a rate on the rate card, or the total isn't positive — a
  sent quote can never be a zero-dollar or partially-rated quote.
  """
  def send_quote(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Quote{} = draft,
        %RateCard{} = rate_card
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    line_items = Pricing.line_items(rate_card, draft)

    if Pricing.finalizable?(line_items) do
      insert_sent_quote(scope, account_id, draft, line_items)
    else
      {:error, :not_finalizable}
    end
  end

  defp insert_sent_quote(scope, account_id, draft, line_items) do
    quote_attrs = %{
      client_id: draft.client_id,
      client_name: draft.client_name,
      client_phone: draft.client_phone,
      pricing_model: draft.pricing_model,
      bedroom_count: draft.bedroom_count,
      bathroom_count: draft.bathroom_count,
      square_feet: draft.square_feet,
      hours: draft.hours,
      status: :sent,
      total_cents: Pricing.total_cents(line_items),
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    }

    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      with {:ok, quote} <-
             %Quote{account_id: account_id} |> Quote.changeset(quote_attrs) |> Repo.insert(),
           {:ok, _items} <- insert_quote_items(quote, line_items) do
        Recorder.record(scope, "quote_sent", "Quote", quote.id, %{}, %{
          "total_cents" => quote.total_cents
        })

        quote
      else
        {:error, changeset} -> Repo.rollback(changeset)
      end
    end)
  end

  defp insert_quote_items(quote, line_items) do
    Enum.reduce_while(line_items, {:ok, []}, fn line_item, {:ok, acc} ->
      case %QuoteItem{quote_id: quote.id} |> QuoteItem.changeset(line_item) |> Repo.insert() do
        {:ok, quote_item} -> {:cont, {:ok, [quote_item | acc]}}
        {:error, _changeset} = error -> {:halt, error}
      end
    end)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t(),
          slug: String.t() | nil,
          drive_time_policy: :unpaid | :paid,
          members: [CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          users: [CleanerCrm.Users.User.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api www help support docs blog)

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "accounts" do
    field :name, :string
    field :slug, :string

    # Whether time spent driving between jobs counts toward a
    # cleaner's pay — read by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` alongside a
    # cleaner's earnings, set here rather than on a separate settings
    # table since it's the account's only pay policy so far.
    field :drive_time_policy, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :paid], default: :unpaid

    has_many :members, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member, on_delete: :delete_all
    has_many :users, through: [:members, :user]

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(account, attrs) do
    account
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :slug, :drive_time_policy])
    |> validate_required([:name])
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 100)
    |> validate_slug()
    |> unique_constraint(:slug)
  end

  def create_changeset(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> changeset(attrs)
    |> maybe_generate_slug()
  end

  defp validate_slug(changeset) do
    changeset
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z0-9-]+$/,
      message: "must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens"
    )
    |> validate_length(:slug, min: 3, max: 50)
    |> validate_exclusion(:slug, @reserved_slugs, message: "is reserved and cannot be used")
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z]/, message: "must start with a letter")
  end

  defp maybe_generate_slug(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :slug) do
      nil ->
        name = get_field(changeset, :name)
        if name, do: put_change(changeset, :slug, generate_slug(name)), else: changeset

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_slug(name) do
    name
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]/, "-")
    |> String.replace(~r/-+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard do
  @moduledoc """
  The account's configurable rates, one per pricing model.

  A single row per account (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card/1`).
  A rate left blank means that pricing model isn't priced yet — quoting
  against it is refused until the owner sets a rate (see
  `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`).

  `weekly_discount_percent`/`biweekly_discount_percent`/`monthly_discount_percent`
  and `add_on_rates_cents` exist for the public instant-quote calculator
  (story 848, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`) — a recurring frequency's
  discount off the one-time subtotal, and the configured price for each
  named add-on (e.g. `"inside_fridge" => 1500`). Unset (`nil`) means no
  discount; an add-on key missing from the map means it isn't priced
  yet, same "never guess a price" rule as the base rates.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          per_sqft_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          weekly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          biweekly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          monthly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          add_on_rates_cents: %{optional(String.t()) => integer()},
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "rate_cards" do
    field :per_room_bedroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_room_bathroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_sqft_rate_cents, :integer
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :weekly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :biweekly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :monthly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :add_on_rates_cents, :map, default: %{}

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @rate_fields ~w(per_room_bedroom_rate_cents per_room_bathroom_rate_cents
                  per_sqft_rate_cents hourly_rate_cents weekly_discount_percent
                  biweekly_discount_percent monthly_discount_percent add_on_rates_cents)a

  @discount_fields ~w(weekly_discount_percent biweekly_discount_percent monthly_discount_percent)a

  def changeset(rate_card, attrs) do
    rate_card
    |> cast(attrs, @rate_fields)
    |> validate_number(:per_room_bedroom_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:per_room_bathroom_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:per_sqft_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:hourly_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_discount_percents()
    |> validate_add_on_rates()
  end

  defp validate_discount_percents(changeset) do
    Enum.reduce(@discount_fields, changeset, fn field, changeset ->
      changeset
      |> validate_number(field, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
      |> validate_number(field, less_than_or_equal_to: 100)
    end)
  end

  # Every configured amount must be a non-negative integer number of
  # cents — the same shape every other rate on this card takes.
  defp validate_add_on_rates(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :add_on_rates_cents) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      rates ->
        if Enum.all?(rates, fn {key, cents} -> is_binary(key) and valid_cents?(cents) end) do
          changeset
        else
          add_error(changeset, :add_on_rates_cents, "must map add-on names to whole cent amounts")
        end
    end
  end

  defp valid_cents?(cents), do: is_integer(cents) and cents >= 0
end

  def total_cents(line_items), do: Enum.reduce(line_items, 0, &(&1.amount_cents + &2))

  @doc "Whether any priced line item is missing a rate from the rate card."
  @spec missing_rate?([line_item()]) :: boolean()
  def missing_rate?(line_items), do: Enum.any?(line_items, &is_nil(&1.rate_cents))

  @doc """
  Whether a quote is ready to send: at least one priced line item,
  every one of them rated, and a positive total.
  """
  @spec finalizable?([line_item()]) :: boolean()
  def finalizable?(line_items) do
    line_items != [] and not missing_rate?(line_items) and total_cents(line_items) > 0
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.update_account(account, attrs) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:updated, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def delete_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.delete_account(account) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:deleted, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def change_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)
    Account.changeset(account, attrs)
  end

  def list_account_members(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.list_account_members(account_id)
  end

  def add_user_to_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:created, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:deleted, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:updated, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.get_user_role(user_id, account_id)
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)
  end

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Invitations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  def subscribe_invitations(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations")
  end

  defp broadcast_invitation(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations", message)
  end

  def invite_user(scope, account_id, email, role)
      when is_binary(email) and role in [:owner, :admin, :member] and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         :ok <- validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id),
         {:ok, invitation} <- create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role),
         :ok <- send_invitation_email(invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:created, invitation})
      {:ok, invitation}
    end
  end

  def accept_invitation(token, user_attrs) when is_binary(token) and is_map(user_attrs) do
    with {:ok, invitation} <- get_valid_invitation(token),
         {:ok, user} <- resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs),
         {:ok, member} <- accept_user_to_account(user, invitation),
         {:ok, _updated} <- InvitationRepository.accept(%Scope{}, invitation) do
      {:ok, {user, member}}
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account_id) do
      InvitationRepository.list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id)
    else
      []
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(_scope, nil), do: []

  def get_invitation_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token)
  end

  def cancel_invitation(scope, account_id, invitation_id)
      when is_integer(invitation_id) and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         invitation when not is_nil(invitation) <-
           InvitationRepository.get_invitation(scope, invitation_id),
         {:ok, cancelled} <- InvitationRepository.cancel(scope, invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:updated, cancelled})
      {:ok, cancelled}
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      error -> error
    end
  end

  def cleanup_expired_invitations do
    InvitationRepository.cleanup_expired_invitations(30)
    :ok
  end

  defp validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:manage_members, scope, account_id),
      do: :ok,
      else: {:error, :not_authorized}
  end

  defp validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id) do
    case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
      nil ->
        :ok

      user ->
        if MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(user.id, account_id),
          do: {:error, :user_already_member},
          else: :ok
    end
  end

  defp create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role) do
    attrs = %{
      email: email,
      role: role,
      account_id: account_id,
      invited_by_user_id: scope.user.id
    }

    InvitationRepository.create_invitation(scope, attrs)
  end

  defp send_invitation_email(invitation) do
    url = CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/invitations/accept/#{invitation.token}"

    case InvitationNotifier.deliver_invitation_email(invitation, url) do
      {:ok, _} -> :ok
      {:error, _} -> {:error, :email_delivery_failed}
    end
  end

  defp get_valid_invitation(token) do
    case InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :invalid_token}

      invitation ->
        cond do
          invitation.status != :pending ->
            {:error, :invalid_token}

          DateTime.compare(DateTime.utc_now(), invitation.expires_at) != :lt ->
            {:error, :expired_token}

          true ->
            {:ok, invitation}
        end
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, %{email: provided_email} = user_attrs) do
    if provided_email == invitation.email do
      case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
        nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs)
        existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
      end
    else
      {:error, :email_mismatch}
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs) do
    user_attrs_with_email = Map.put(user_attrs, :email, invitation.email)

    case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
      nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs_with_email)
      existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
    end
  end

  defp accept_user_to_account(user, invitation) do
    inviter = Users.get_user!(invitation.invited_by_user_id)
    inviter_scope = %Scope{user: inviter, active_account_id: invitation.account_id}
    add_user_to_account(inviter_scope, user.id, invitation.account_id, invitation.role)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.AccountsRepository do
  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, Member}

  def create_account(attrs) do
    %Account{}
    |> Account.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def get_account(id), do: Repo.get(Account, id)
  def get_account!(id), do: Repo.get!(Account, id)

  def update_account(%Account{} = account, attrs) do
    account
    |> Account.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def delete_account(%Account{} = account), do: Repo.delete(account)

  def create_account_with_owner(attrs, owner_id) do
    Repo.transaction(fn ->
      with {:ok, account} <- create_account(attrs),
           {:ok, _member} <-
             create_member(%{user_id: owner_id, account_id: account.id, role: :owner}) do
        account
      else
        {:error, reason} -> Repo.rollback(reason)
      end
    end)
  end

  def by_slug(slug), do: from(a in Account, where: a.slug == ^slug)
  def with_preloads(preloads), do: preload(Account, ^preloads)

  defp create_member(attrs) do
    %Member{}
    |> Member.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end
end
