1 defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.SettingsLive.BookingPolicy do 2 @moduledoc """ 3 Owner-only editor for the account's `CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy` 4 (story 851 follow-up, issue db25b304): the notice-window hours, the 5 late and same-day cancellation fees, and the policy text shown to a 6 client at booking and in their portal. Before this page existed, 7 the only way to set any of it was a direct database edit. 8 9 Fees are entered in dollars and converted to cents before they ever 10 reach the changeset — `CancellationPolicy` itself only stores 11 integer cents — mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.RateCard`'s own 12 rate inputs. 13 14 An account with no saved policy yet edits the same fresh, unsaved, 15 all-zero-fee default that `CleanerCrm.Portal.get_cancellation_policy/1` 16 hands the portal itself — the portal keeps working with those 17 defaults whether or not this page has ever been visited. 18 19 ## Route 20 21 * `/app/settings/booking` (`:edit`) — office-only, gated the same as 22 every other office surface (`CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`). 23 24 ## Dependencies 25 26 - `CleanerCrm.Portal` 27 """ 28 29 use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view 30 31 alias CleanerCrm.Portal 32 alias CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy 33 34 @impl true 35 def render(assigns) do 36 ~H""" 37 38 <.header> 39 Cancellation Policy 40 <:subtitle> 41 Notice window and fees enforced on self-service reschedule/cancel in the client portal 42 43 44 45 <.form 46 for={@form} 47 id="cancellation-policy-form" 48 data-test="cancellation-policy-form" 49 phx-change="validate" 50 phx-submit="save" 51 > 52
53
54 <.input 55 field={@form[:notice_window_hours]} 56 type="number" 57 min="0" 58 label="Notice window (hours)" 59 data-test="notice-window-input" 60 /> 61

62 How much notice a client must give to cancel or reschedule free of the late fee. 63

64 65 <.input 66 type="number" 67 step="0.01" 68 min="0" 69 name="policy[late_fee]" 70 id={@form[:late_fee_cents].id} 71 label="Late cancellation fee ($)" 72 value={@fee_inputs.late_fee} 73 errors={field_errors(@form[:late_fee_cents])} 74 data-test="late-fee-input" 75 /> 76 <.input 77 type="number" 78 step="0.01" 79 min="0" 80 name="policy[same_day_fee]" 81 id={@form[:same_day_fee_cents].id} 82 label="Same-day cancellation fee ($)" 83 value={@fee_inputs.same_day_fee} 84 errors={field_errors(@form[:same_day_fee_cents])} 85 data-test="same-day-fee-input" 86 /> 87

88 Charged instead of the late fee when a visit is cancelled the same day it's scheduled. 89

90 91 <.input 92 field={@form[:policy_text]} 93 type="textarea" 94 label="Policy text shown to clients" 95 data-test="policy-text-input" 96 /> 97
98
99 100
101 <.button 102 phx-disable-with="Saving..." 103 variant="primary" 104 data-test="save-cancellation-policy-button" 105 > 106 Save Policy 107 108
109 110 111 """ 112 end 113 114 @impl true 115 def mount(_params, _session, socket) do 116 scope = socket.assigns.current_scope 117 policy = Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id) 118 119 {:ok, 120 socket 121 |> assign(:page_title, "Cancellation Policy") 122 |> assign(:policy, policy) 123 |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs(policy)) 124 |> assign(:form, to_form(Portal.change_cancellation_policy(scope, policy), as: :policy))} 125 end 126 127 @impl true 128 def handle_event("validate", %{"policy" => params}, socket) do 129 {:noreply, apply_params(socket, params, :validate)} 130 end 131 132 def handle_event("save", %{"policy" => params}, socket) do 133 scope = socket.assigns.current_scope 134 {attrs, fee_inputs} = build_attrs(params) 135 136 case Portal.set_cancellation_policy(scope, attrs) do 137 {:ok, updated} -> 138 {:noreply, 139 socket 140 |> put_flash(:info, "Cancellation policy updated.") 141 |> assign(:policy, updated) 142 |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs(updated)) 143 |> assign(:form, to_form(Portal.change_cancellation_policy(scope, updated), as: :policy))} 144 145 {:error, changeset} -> 146 {:noreply, 147 socket 148 |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs) 149 |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :policy))} 150 end 151 end 152 153 defp apply_params(socket, params, action) do 154 {attrs, fee_inputs} = build_attrs(params) 155 156 changeset = 157 socket.assigns.current_scope 158 |> Portal.change_cancellation_policy(socket.assigns.policy, attrs) 159 |> Map.put(:action, action) 160 161 socket 162 |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs) 163 |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :policy)) 164 end 165 166 # Builds the changeset attrs (dollar inputs converted to cents) 167 # alongside the raw dollar strings to redisplay — the same pair 168 # both `validate` and `save` need, so both event handlers go through 169 # here, mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.RateCard#build_attrs/2`. 170 defp build_attrs(params) do 171 fee_inputs = %{ 172 late_fee: Map.get(params, "late_fee", ""), 173 same_day_fee: Map.get(params, "same_day_fee", "") 174 } 175 176 attrs = %{ 177 "notice_window_hours" => Map.get(params, "notice_window_hours"), 178 "late_fee_cents" => dollars_to_cents(fee_inputs.late_fee), 179 "same_day_fee_cents" => dollars_to_cents(fee_inputs.same_day_fee), 180 "policy_text" => Map.get(params, "policy_text") 181 } 182 183 {attrs, fee_inputs} 184 end 185 186 defp fee_inputs(%CancellationPolicy{} = policy) do 187 %{ 188 late_fee: cents_to_dollars(policy.late_fee_cents), 189 same_day_fee: cents_to_dollars(policy.same_day_fee_cents) 190 } 191 end 192 193 defp cents_to_dollars(nil), do: "" 194 195 defp cents_to_dollars(cents), 196 do: cents |> Decimal.new() |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100)) |> Decimal.to_string(:normal) 197 198 #     51	  end

   126	  end
   127	end

     2	  use Ecto.Schema
     3	  import Ecto.Changeset
     4	  import Ecto.Query
     5	
     6	  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
     7	          id: integer(),
     8	          role: :owner | :admin | :member,
     9	          user_id: integer(),
    10	          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t(),
    11	          user: CleanerCrm.Users.User.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
    12	          account: CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
    13	          inserted_at: NaiveDateTime.t(),
    14	          updated_at: NaiveDateTime.t()
    15	        }
    16	
    17	  schema "members" do
    18	    field :role, Ecto.Enum, values: [:owner, :admin, :member], default: :member
    19	
    20	    belongs_to :user, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    21	    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    22	
    23	    timestamps()
    24	  end
    25	
    26	  def changeset(member, attrs) do
    27	    member
    28	    |> cast(attrs, [:role, :user_id, :account_id])
    29	    |> validate_required([:role, :user_id, :account_id])
    30	    |> validate_inclusion(:role, [:owner, :admin, :member])
    31	    |> assoc_constraint(:user)
    32	    |> assoc_constraint(:account)
    33	    |> unique_constraint([:user_id, :account_id], name: :members_user_id_account_id_index)
    34	  end
    35	
    36	  def update_role_changeset(member, attrs) do
    37	    member
    38	    |> cast(attrs, [:role])
    39	    |> validate_required([:role])
    40	    |> validate_inclusion(:role, [:owner, :admin, :member])
    41	  end
    42	
    43	  def validate_owner_exists(changeset, repo) do
    44	    case get_field(changeset, :role) do
    45	      :owner ->
    46	        changeset
    47	
    48	      _ ->
    49	        user_id = get_field(changeset, :user_id)
    50	        account_id = get_field(changeset, :account_id)
    51	
    52	        if user_id && account_id do
    53	          case repo.get_by(__MODULE__, user_id: user_id, account_id: account_id) do
    54	            %{role: :owner} ->
    55	              owner_count =
    56	                repo.aggregate(
    57	                  from(m in __MODULE__, where: m.account_id == ^account_id and m.role == :owner),
    58	                  :count
    59	                )
    60	
    61	              if owner_count <= 1 do
    62	                add_error(changeset, :role, "account must have at least one owner")
    63	              else
    64	                changeset
    65	              end
    66	
    67	            _ ->
    68	              changeset
    69	          end
    70	        else
    71	          changeset
    72	        end
    73	    end
    74	  end
    75	
    76	  def has_role?(member, required_role) do
    77	    role_hierarchy = %{member: 1, admin: 2, owner: 3}
    78	    Map.get(role_hierarchy, member.role, 0) >= Map.get(role_hierarchy, required_role, 0)
    79	  end
    80	
    81	  def owner?(member), do: member.role == :owner
    82	  def admin_or_owner?(member), do: member.role in [:admin, :owner]
    83	end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.User do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  schema "users" do
    field :email, :string
    field :name, :string
    field :password, :string, virtual: true, redact: true
    field :hashed_password, :string, redact: true
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime
    field :authenticated_at, :utc_datetime, virtual: true
    field :push_enabled, :boolean, default: true

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime)
  end

  @doc """
  A user changeset for registering or changing the email.

  It requires the email to change otherwise an error is added.

  Also casts `:push_enabled` — there's no dedicated settings changeset
  for it, and this is the only changeset `register_user/1` runs, so
  it's the one path that lets a cleaner fixture seed the preference.

  ## Options

    * `:validate_unique` - Set to false if you don't want to validate the
      uniqueness of the email, useful when displaying live validations.
      Defaults to `true`.
  """
  def email_changeset(user, attrs, opts \\ []) do
    user
    |> cast(attrs, [:email, :push_enabled])
    |> validate_email(opts)
  end

  defp validate_email(changeset, opts) do
    changeset =
      changeset
      |> validate_required([:email])
      |> validate_format(:email, ~r/^[^@,;\s]+@[^@,;\s]+$/,
        message: "must have the @ sign and no spaces"
      )
      |> validate_length(:email, max: 160)

    if Keyword.get(opts, :validate_unique, true) do
      changeset
      |> unsafe_validate_unique(:email, CleanerCrm.Repo)
      |> unique_constraint(:email)
      |> validate_email_changed()
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  defp validate_email_changed(changeset) do
    if get_field(changeset, :email) && get_change(changeset, :email) == nil do
      add_error(changeset, :email, "did not change")
    else

defmodule CleanerCrm.BookingTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 4e985412: `/book/accept/:token`'s slot-selection form
  accepted any date — including years in the past — with zero
  validation, and QA drove a `scheduled_date` of 2020-01-01 all the
  way through card capture into a real scheduled job. Both guards
  added for it are exercised here:

    * `Lead.slot_changeset/3` (via `Booking.select_slot/3`) — the
      form-level guard, rejecting a past date/time outright.
    * `Booking.confirm_booking/3` — the defense-in-depth re-check
      right before a card is charged, in case a slot that was future
      at selection time goes stale (or a lead's slot fields were set
      some other way) by the time the client actually submits payment.

  No spex/BDD story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead,
  mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.TemplatesTest`'s precedent for
  issue-only coverage.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      Booking.create_lead(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  describe "select_slot/3" do
    test "rejects a scheduled_date years in the past" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => "2020-01-01",
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert "must be today or later" in errors_on(changeset).scheduled_date
    end

    test "rejects today's date once the chosen start time has already passed" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      today = Date.utc_today()
      now = DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(
                 lead,
                 %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
                 now
               )

      assert "must be later than the current time" in errors_on(changeset).start_time
    end

    test "accepts a future date" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      future_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)

      assert {:ok, slotted} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(future_date),
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert slotted.scheduled_date == future_date
    end
  end

  describe "confirm_booking/3 (defense in depth against a past slot)" do
    test "refuses a lead whose slot fields are already in the past, without charging a card" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      past_lead = %{lead | scheduled_date: ~D[2020-01-01], start_time: ~T[09:00:00]}

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(past_lead, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
      assert reloaded.status == :accepted
      assert reloaded.stripe_payment_intent_id == nil
    end

    test "refuses a slot picked for later today once that time has passed by confirmation" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      today = Date.utc_today()

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(
          lead,
          %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
          DateTime.new!(today, ~T[13:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
        )

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(
                 slotted,
                 %{"policy_agreed" => "true", "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"},
                 DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
               )
    end

    test "still confirms and moves the lead to payment_pending for a genuinely future slot" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
          "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
          "start_time" => "09:00"
        })

      assert {:ok, updated} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(slotted, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      assert updated.status == :payment_pending
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story848.Criterion7215Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 848 — Get an instant quote from the public website
  Criterion 7215 — Building a quote with room counts shows a price
  with no contact info: a real price is shown from selecting a
  service type and room counts alone, before any name, email, or
  phone is entered.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the public quote form prices a per-room home before contact info is given" do
    scenario "building a quote with room counts shows a price with no contact info" do
      given_ "a business with a per-room rate card and a visitor on the public quote page",
             context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        Fixtures.account_fixture(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Clean Co"})

        Fixtures.rate_card_fixture(scope, %{
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 5000,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: 3000
        })

        {:ok, quote_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/book")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :quote_live, quote_live)}
      end

      when_ "the visitor selects a service type, bedroom count, and bathroom count without entering a name, email, or phone",
            context do
        html =
          context.quote_live

      then_ "a real price computed from the rate card is displayed immediately", context do
        assert has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$210.00")
        refute has_element?(context.quote_live, "[data-test='unsupported-quote-message']")

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Booking,
              CleanerCrm.Portal,
              CleanerCrm.Reviews
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    # `CleanerCrm.Users.register_user/1` (which `user_fixture/1` goes
    # through) only ever casts `:email` and `:push_enabled` — the
  end

  # Quoting (story 848) — the account's public-facing rate card, set
  # directly rather than through the office `QuoteLive.Builder` rate
  # card form (covered end-to-end by story 835) since these specs'
  # subject is the public instant-quote calculator reading it, not the
  # office save flow. Extra keys the current `RateCard` schema doesn't
  # persist yet (frequency discounts, add-on pricing) are accepted
  # here so specs can drive the pricing config story 848 needs once
  # the schema grows to hold it.
  def rate_card_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    rate_card = CleanerCrm.Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)
    {:ok, rate_card} = CleanerCrm.Quoting.update_rate_card(scope, rate_card, attrs)
    rate_card
  end

  # Booking (story 849) — an instant quote already accepted by the
  # client (contact captured, price locked). The quote-to-accepted
  # transition itself is covered end-to-end by story 848's own
  # "instant quote price matches the later acceptance total" spec, so
  # scenarios whose subject is the slot/policy/card steps that follow
  # seed the accepted lead directly here instead of re-driving the
  # quote calculator every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      CleanerCrm.Booking.create_lead(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.SettingsLive.BookingPolicyTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue db25b304: no owner UI ever edited
  `CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy` — only a direct database edit
  reached the notice-window hours, late/same-day fees, or policy text
  the client portal enforces and displays.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp log_in(conn, scope), do: log_in_user(conn, scope.user)

  test "renders the account's current policy, defaulting to zero fees when unset", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()

    {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='notice-window-input']")
    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='late-fee-input']")
    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='same-day-fee-input']")
    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='policy-text-input']")
  end

  test "saves notice window, fees, and policy text, converting dollars to cents", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    lv
    |> form("[data-test='cancellation-policy-form']",
      policy: %{
        notice_window_hours: "48",
        late_fee: "25.00",
        same_day_fee: "75.50",
        policy_text: "Cancel 48 hours ahead to avoid a fee."
      }
    )
    |> render_submit()

    policy = Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id)

    assert policy.notice_window_hours == 48
    assert policy.late_fee_cents == 2_500
    assert policy.same_day_fee_cents == 7_550
    assert policy.policy_text == "Cancel 48 hours ahead to avoid a fee."
  end

  test "an existing saved policy is preloaded into the form for editing", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()

    {:ok, _policy} =
      Portal.set_cancellation_policy(scope, %{
        notice_window_hours: 24,
        late_fee_cents: 1_000,
        same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
      })

    {:ok, lv, html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    assert html =~ "value=\"10\""
    assert html =~ "value=\"50\""

    lv
    |> form("[data-test='cancellation-policy-form']",
      policy: %{late_fee: "12.00"}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    assert Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id).late_fee_cents == 1_200
  end

  test "rejects a negative notice window", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    html =
      lv
      |> form("[data-test='cancellation-policy-form']",
        policy: %{notice_window_hours: "-5", late_fee: "10.00", same_day_fee: "20.00"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

    assert html =~ "must be greater than or equal to"
    assert Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id).notice_window_hours == 24
  end
end

  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}

  defp log_in(conn, scope), do: log_in_user(conn, scope.user)

  test "renders the current rate card's base rates, discounts, and add-ons", %{conn: conn} do

    {:ok, _rate_card} =
      Quoting.update_rate_card(scope, Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope), %{
        per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 3500,

1 defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Accept do 2 @moduledoc """ 3 Token-link quote acceptance (story 849): the locked price recap, 4 slot selection, cancellation-policy agreement, and card capture that 5 converts a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead` into a client + property + 6 plan/job and issues portal access. 7 8 Mounted as the `:accept` `live_action` of 9 `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` rather than routed on its own — 10 see that module's moduledoc for why (`push_patch/2` only navigates 11 within the currently-mounted view module, and the calculator patches 12 here once contact info locks in a price). Every function below still 13 only ever touches `CleanerCrm.Booking`. 14 15 ## Dependencies 16 17 - `CleanerCrm.Booking` 18 """ 19 20 use CleanerCrmWeb, :html 21 22 require Logger 23 24 alias CleanerCrm.Booking 25 alias CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead 26 alias CleanerCrm.Money 27 28 @doc "Loads the lead for `token` and sets up whichever step it's currently at." 29 def mount(token, socket) do 30 case Booking.get_lead_by_token(token) do 31 nil -> 32 socket 33 |> assign(:page_title, "Booking not found") 34 |> assign(:step, :not_found) 35 |> assign(:lead, nil) 36 37 %Lead{} = lead -> 38 socket 39 |> assign(:page_title, "Confirm your booking") 40 |> assign(:lead, lead) 41 |> assign(:slot_form, to_form(Booking.change_slot(lead), as: :booking)) 42 |> assign(:confirmation_form, to_form(Booking.change_confirmation(lead), as: :booking)) 43 |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false) 44 |> assign(:policy_required, false) 45 |> assign(:step, step_for(lead)) 46 end 47 end 48 49 defp step_for(%Lead{status: :converted}), do: :confirmed 50 defp step_for(%Lead{status: :payment_pending}), do: :payment_pending 51 defp step_for(%Lead{status: :payment_declined}), do: :payment_declined 52 defp step_for(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: :select_slot 53 defp step_for(%Lead{}), do: :confirm 54 55 def render(assigns) do 56 ~H""" 57 58 <.header>Confirm your booking 59 60

61 We couldn't find that booking link. It may have expired — please request a new quote. 62

63 64
65
66

Your price

67

68 {Money.format_cents(@lead.total_cents)} 69

70

71 Locked in from your instant quote — no added fees. 72

73
74
75 76
77 78 You're booked for {format_date(@lead.scheduled_date)} at {format_time(@lead.start_time)}. 79 Check your email for a link to your client portal. 80 81
82 83
84 Confirming your payment — this page will update as soon as it's done. 85
86 87
88
93 Your card was declined. Please try a different card below. 94
95 96
97 That time was just booked by someone else — please pick another slot. 98
99 100 <.form 101 :if={@step == :select_slot} 102 for={@slot_form} 103 id="slot-form" 104 data-test="slot-form" 105 phx-submit="select_slot" 106 > 107 <.input field={@slot_form[:scheduled_date]} type="date" label="Date" /> 108 <.input field={@slot_form[:start_time]} type="time" label="Start time" /> 109 110
111 <.button phx-disable-with="Checking...">Continue 112
113 114 115 <.form 116 :if={@step in [:confirm, :payment_declined]} 117 for={@confirmation_form} 118 id="confirmation-form" 119 data-test="confirmation-form" 120 phx-submit="confirm_booking" 121 > 122

123 Cancellation policy: cancel or reschedule at least 24-hour ahead of your visit to 124 avoid a late-cancellation fee. 125

126 127 <.input 128 field={@confirmation_form[:policy_agreed]} 129 type="checkbox" 130 label="I agree to the cancellation policy" 131 data-test="policy-agreement-checkbox" 132 /> 133

134 Please agree to the cancellation policy to continue. 135

136 137 <%!-- 138 Real card capture (Stripe Elements) is deferred — this 139 mirrors the existing `/pay/:token` payment page's own 140 simplification, a single test card baked in as a hidden 141 field until Elements lands. 142 --%> 143 144 145
146 <.button phx-disable-with="Booking..."> 147 Confirm & pay {Money.format_cents(@lead.total_cents)} 148 149
150 151

Mounted as the `:accept` `live_action` of `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` rather than routed on its own — see that module's moduledoc for why (`push_patch/2` only navigates within the currently-mounted view module, and the calculator patches here once contact info locks in a price). Every function below still only ever touches `CleanerCrm.Booking`. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Booking` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :html require Logger alias CleanerCrm.Booking alias CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead alias CleanerCrm.Money @doc "Loads the lead for `token` and sets up whichever step it's currently at." def mount(token, socket) do case Booking.get_lead_by_token(token) do nil -> socket |> assign(:page_title, "Booking not found") |> assign(:step, :not_found) |> assign(:lead, nil) %Lead{} = lead -> socket |> assign(:page_title, "Confirm your booking") |> assign(:lead, lead) |> assign(:slot_form, to_form(Booking.change_slot(lead), as: :booking)) |> assign(:confirmation_form, to_form(Booking.change_confirmation(lead), as: :booking)) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false) |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:step, step_for(lead)) end end defp step_for(%Lead{status: :converted}), do: :confirmed defp step_for(%Lead{status: :payment_pending}), do: :payment_pending defp step_for(%Lead{status: :payment_declined}), do: :payment_declined defp step_for(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: :select_slot defp step_for(%Lead{}), do: :confirm def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header>Confirm your booking

We couldn't find that booking link. It may have expired — please request a new quote.

Your price

{Money.format_cents(@lead.total_cents)}

Locked in from your instant quote — no added fees.

You're booked for {format_date(@lead.scheduled_date)} at {format_time(@lead.start_time)}. Check your email for a link to your client portal.
Confirming your payment — this page will update as soon as it's done.
Your card was declined. Please try a different card below.
That time was just booked by someone else — please pick another slot.
<.form :if={@step == :select_slot} for={@slot_form} id="slot-form" data-test="slot-form" phx-submit="select_slot" > <.input field={@slot_form[:scheduled_date]} type="date" label="Date" /> <.input field={@slot_form[:start_time]} type="time" label="Start time" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Checking...">Continue
<.form :if={@step in [:confirm, :payment_declined]} for={@confirmation_form} id="confirmation-form" data-test="confirmation-form" phx-submit="confirm_booking" >

Cancellation policy: cancel or reschedule at least 24-hour ahead of your visit to avoid a late-cancellation fee.

<.input field={@confirmation_form[:policy_agreed]} type="checkbox" label="I agree to the cancellation policy" data-test="policy-agreement-checkbox" />

Please agree to the cancellation policy to continue.

<.button phx-disable-with="Booking..."> Confirm & pay {Money.format_cents(@lead.total_cents)}
""" end def handle_event("select_slot", %{"booking" => params}, socket) do case Booking.select_slot(socket.assigns.lead, params) do {:ok, slotted_lead} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:lead, slotted_lead) |> assign(:step, :confirm)} {:error, changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :slot_form, to_form(changeset, as: :booking))} end end def handle_event("confirm_booking", %{"booking" => params}, socket) do case Booking.confirm_booking(socket.assigns.lead, params) do {:ok, updated} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:lead, updated) |> assign(:step, :payment_pending) |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false)} {:error, :policy_required} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:policy_required, true) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false)} {:error, :slot_unavailable} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:slot_unavailable, true) |> assign(:policy_required, false)} # Defense in depth (issue 4e985412): the slot-selection form # itself now rejects a past date/time, but a slot picked as # "later today" can still go stale by the time the client # reaches this step — send them back to pick a new one rather # than leave them stuck retrying a confirmation that can never # succeed. {:error, :slot_in_past} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:step, :select_slot) |> assign(:slot_form, to_form(Booking.change_slot(socket.assigns.lead), as: :booking)) |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false) |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash( :error, "That time has already passed — please pick another slot." )} # Anything else is a payment/system failure, NOT a slot conflict — # mislabeling it as "someone else booked this" sends the client # hunting for a new time that will fail identically. {:error, reason} -> Logger.error( "Booking confirmation failed for lead #{socket.assigns.lead.id}: " <> inspect(reason) ) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false) |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash( :error, "We could not process your payment. defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account do
  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t(),
          slug: String.t() | nil,
          drive_time_policy: :unpaid | :paid,
          members: [CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          users: [CleanerCrm.Users.User.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api www help support docs blog)

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "accounts" do
    field :name, :string
    field :slug, :string

    # Whether time spent driving between jobs counts toward a
    # cleaner's pay — read by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` alongside a
    # cleaner's earnings, set here rather than on a separate settings
    # table since it's the account's only pay policy so far.
    field :drive_time_policy, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :paid], default: :unpaid

    has_many :members, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Member, on_delete: :delete_all
    has_many :users, through: [:members, :user]

    timestamps()
  end

  def changeset(account, attrs) do
    account
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :slug, :drive_time_policy])
    |> validate_required([:name])
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 100)
    |> validate_slug()
    |> unique_constraint(:slug)
  end

  def create_changeset(attrs) do
    %__MODULE__{}
    |> changeset(attrs)
    |> maybe_generate_slug()
  end

  defp validate_slug(changeset) do
    changeset
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z0-9-]+$/,
      message: "must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens"
    )
    |> validate_length(:slug, min: 3, max: 50)
    |> validate_exclusion(:slug, @reserved_slugs, message: "is reserved and cannot be used")
    |> validate_format(:slug, ~r/^[a-z]/, message: "must start with a letter")
  end

  defp maybe_generate_slug(changeset) do
    case get_field(changeset, :slug) do
      nil ->
        name = get_field(changeset, :name)
        if name, do: put_change(changeset, :slug, generate_slug(name)), else: changeset

      _ ->
        changeset
    end
  end

  defp generate_slug(name) do
    name
    |> String.downcase()
    |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]/, "-")
    |> String.replace(~r/-+/, "-")
    |> String.trim("-")
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Accounts do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{Account, AccountsRepository, MembersRepository}
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.{InvitationRepository, InvitationNotifier}
  alias CleanerCrm.Authorization
  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def subscribe_account(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account")
  end

  def subscribe_member(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member")
  end

  defp broadcast_account(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:account", message)
  end

  defp broadcast_member(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:member", message)
  end

  def list_accounts(%Scope{} = scope) do
    MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(scope.user.id)
  end

  def get_account(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    case AccountsRepository.get_account(id) do
      nil ->
        nil

      account ->
        case Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account.id) do
          false -> nil
          true -> account
        end
    end
  end

  def get_account!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    account = AccountsRepository.get_account!(id)
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account.id)
    account
  end

  def create_account(%Scope{} = scope, attrs) do
    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.create_account_with_owner(attrs, scope.user.id) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:created, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def update_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.update_account(account, attrs) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:updated, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def delete_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)

    with {:ok, account} <- AccountsRepository.delete_account(account) do
      broadcast_account(scope, {:deleted, account})
      {:ok, account}
    end
  end

  def change_account(%Scope{} = scope, %Account{} = account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account.id)
    Account.changeset(account, attrs)
  end

  def list_account_members(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.list_account_members(account_id)
  end

  def add_user_to_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role \\ :member) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_account, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.add_user_to_account(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:created, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def remove_user_from_account(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.remove_user_from_account(user_id, account_id) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:deleted, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def update_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id, role) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:manage_members, scope, account_id)

    with {:ok, member} <- MembersRepository.update_user_role(user_id, account_id, role) do
      broadcast_member(scope, {:updated, member})
      {:ok, member}
    end
  end

  def get_user_role(%Scope{} = scope, user_id, account_id) do
    Authorization.authorize!(:read_account, scope, account_id)
    MembersRepository.get_user_role(user_id, account_id)
  end

  def user_has_account_access?(%Scope{} = scope, account_id) do
    MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)
  end

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Invitations
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  def subscribe_invitations(%Scope{} = scope) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.subscribe(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations")
  end

  defp broadcast_invitation(%Scope{} = scope, message) do
    key = scope.user.id
    Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast(CleanerCrm.PubSub, "user:#{key}:invitations", message)
  end

  def invite_user(scope, account_id, email, role)
      when is_binary(email) and role in [:owner, :admin, :member] and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         :ok <- validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id),
         {:ok, invitation} <- create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role),
         :ok <- send_invitation_email(invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:created, invitation})
      {:ok, invitation}
    end
  end

  def accept_invitation(token, user_attrs) when is_binary(token) and is_map(user_attrs) do
    with {:ok, invitation} <- get_valid_invitation(token),
         {:ok, user} <- resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs),
         {:ok, member} <- accept_user_to_account(user, invitation),
         {:ok, _updated} <- InvitationRepository.accept(%Scope{}, invitation) do
      {:ok, {user, member}}
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:read_account, scope, account_id) do
      InvitationRepository.list_pending_invitations(scope, account_id)
    else
      []
    end
  end

  def list_pending_invitations(_scope, nil), do: []

  def get_invitation_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token)
  end

  def cancel_invitation(scope, account_id, invitation_id)
      when is_integer(invitation_id) and not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id),
         invitation when not is_nil(invitation) <-
           InvitationRepository.get_invitation(scope, invitation_id),
         {:ok, cancelled} <- InvitationRepository.cancel(scope, invitation) do
      broadcast_invitation(scope, {:updated, cancelled})
      {:ok, cancelled}
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      error -> error
    end
  end

  def cleanup_expired_invitations do
    InvitationRepository.cleanup_expired_invitations(30)
    :ok
  end

  defp validate_manage_members_permission(scope, account_id) do
    if Authorization.authorize(:manage_members, scope, account_id),
      do: :ok,
      else: {:error, :not_authorized}
  end

  defp validate_user_not_already_member(email, account_id) do
    case Users.get_user_by_email(email) do
      nil ->
        :ok

      user ->
        if MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(user.id, account_id),
          do: {:error, :user_already_member},
          else: :ok
    end
  end

  defp create_invitation(scope, account_id, email, role) do
    attrs = %{
      email: email,
      role: role,
      account_id: account_id,
      invited_by_user_id: scope.user.id
    }

    InvitationRepository.create_invitation(scope, attrs)
  end

  defp send_invitation_email(invitation) do
    url = CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> "/invitations/accept/#{invitation.token}"

    case InvitationNotifier.deliver_invitation_email(invitation, url) do
      {:ok, _} -> :ok
      {:error, _} -> {:error, :email_delivery_failed}
    end
  end

  defp get_valid_invitation(token) do
    case InvitationRepository.get_by_token_hash(token) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :invalid_token}

      invitation ->
        cond do
          invitation.status != :pending ->
            {:error, :invalid_token}

          DateTime.compare(DateTime.utc_now(), invitation.expires_at) != :lt ->
            {:error, :expired_token}

          true ->
            {:ok, invitation}
        end
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, %{email: provided_email} = user_attrs) do
    if provided_email == invitation.email do
      case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
        nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs)
        existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
      end
    else
      {:error, :email_mismatch}
    end
  end

  defp resolve_or_create_user(invitation, user_attrs) do
    user_attrs_with_email = Map.put(user_attrs, :email, invitation.email)

    case Users.get_user_by_email(invitation.email) do
      nil -> Users.register_user(user_attrs_with_email)
      existing_user -> {:ok, existing_user}
    end
  end

  defp accept_user_to_account(user, invitation) do
    inviter = Users.get_user!(invitation.invited_by_user_id)
    inviter_scope = %Scope{user: inviter, active_account_id: invitation.account_id}
    add_user_to_account(inviter_scope, user.id, invitation.account_id, invitation.role)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead do
  @moduledoc """
  A public instant-quote submission (story 848/849): the property
  inputs and frequency/add-ons it was priced from, the price snapshot
  frozen at the moment contact info was captured, the client's contact
  details, and everything the acceptance flow (slot, cancellation-policy
  agreement, card) adds on top of it.

  ## Status

  `:quoted` — never actually persisted today (the calculator on `/book`
  prices a lead purely in memory, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.change_lead/2`)
  but kept as the schema default for a row that, in principle, exists
  before contact info locks it in.

  `:accepted` -> `:payment_pending` -> `:converted`, or `:payment_pending`
  -> `:payment_declined` (from which the client can retry). Only a
  Stripe webhook (`CleanerCrm.Booking.receive_payment_webhook/1`) ever
  moves a lead into `:converted` or `:payment_declined` — submitting
  the card just moves it to `:payment_pending`, per the same
  webhook-confirms-everything rule `CleanerCrm.Billing` follows for
  invoice payments.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type pricing_model :: :per_room | :per_sqft | :hourly
  @type frequency :: :one_time | :weekly | :biweekly | :monthly
  @type status :: :quoted | :accepted | :payment_pending | :payment_declined | :converted

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          pricing_model: pricing_model() | nil,
          bedroom_count: integer() | nil,
          bathroom_count: integer() | nil,
          square_feet: integer() | nil,
          hours: integer() | nil,
          frequency: frequency(),
          add_ons: [String.t()],
          total_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          client_name: String.t() | nil,
          client_email: String.t() | nil,
          client_phone: String.t() | nil,
          acceptance_token: String.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          policy_agreed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          policy_agreed: boolean() | nil,
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "leads" do
    field :pricing_model, Ecto.Enum, values: [:per_room, :per_sqft, :hourly]
    field :bedroom_count, :integer
    field :bathroom_count, :integer
    field :square_feet, :integer
    field :hours, :integer

    field :frequency, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:one_time, :weekly, :biweekly, :monthly],
      default: :one_time

    field :add_ons, {:array, :string}, default: []
    field :total_cents, :integer

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:quoted, :accepted, :payment_pending, :payment_declined, :converted],
      default: :quoted

    field :client_name, :string
    field :client_email, :string
    field :client_phone, :string

    field :acceptance_token, :string

    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time
    field :policy_agreed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    # Not persisted as a boolean column — `confirm_booking/2` turns a
    # truthy submission into `policy_agreed_at` instead. Only exists so
    # the confirmation form has a real changeset field to bind its
    # agreement checkbox to.
    field :policy_agreed, :boolean, virtual: true, default: false

    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @quote_fields ~w(pricing_model bedroom_count bathroom_count square_feet hours frequency add_ons)a

  @doc """
  The calculator's own changeset — every pricing input, none of it
  required, so `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing` can price a live preview
  (via `Ecto.Changeset.apply_changes/1`) after every keystroke
  regardless of whether the changeset is complete yet.
  """
  def quote_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> cast(normalize_add_ons(attrs), @quote_fields)
    |> validate_number(:bedroom_count, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:bathroom_count, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:square_feet, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:hours, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
  end

  @doc """
  The full changeset used once a lead is actually persisted: the
  calculator's inputs plus the price snapshot, contact details, and
  every field the acceptance flow fills in afterward.
  """
  def changeset(lead, attrs) do
    lead
    |> quote_changeset(attrs)
    |> cast(attrs, [
      :total_cents,
      :status,
      :client_name,
      :client_email,
      :client_phone,
      :acceptance_token,
      :scheduled_date,
      :start_time,
      :end_time,
      :policy_agreed_at,
      :stripe_payment_intent_id,
      :client_id,
      :property_id,
      :job_id,
      :recurring_plan_id
    ])
    |> validate_required([:client_name, :client_email, :client_phone], message: "is required")
    |> validate_number(:total_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:acceptance_token)
  end

  @doc """
  The slot-selection step's own changeset — the chosen date and start
  time, required and rejected outright if already in the past (issue
  4e985412: this form accepted any date, including years-old ones,
  with zero validation). `now` defaults to the real clock but takes an
  override so callers can test the boundary without sleeping.
  """
  def slot_changeset(lead, attrs, now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    lead
    |> cast(attrs, [:scheduled_date, :start_time])
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time], message: "is required")
    |> validate_slot_in_future(now)
  end

  @doc "The confirmation step's own changeset — the policy-agreement checkbox."
  def confirmation_changeset(lead, attrs) do
    cast(lead, attrs, [:policy_agreed])
  end

  @doc """
  Whether a lead's `scheduled_date`/`start_time` are still ahead of
  `now` (defaulting to the real clock) — today counts only if
  `start_time` hasn't passed yet. `false` for either field unset.

  The single source of truth behind two checks: `slot_changeset/3`'s
  own validation above (the form-level guard), and
  `CleanerCrm.Booking.confirm_booking/3`'s defense-in-depth re-check
  right before a card is charged — a slot picked as "later today" can
  go stale by the time the client actually submits payment, the same
  reason `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.slot_available?/4` gets re-checked
  there too.
  """
  @spec slot_in_future?(t(), DateTime.t()) :: boolean()
  def slot_in_future?(lead, now \\ DateTime.utc_now())

  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: nil}, _now), do: false
  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{start_time: nil}, _now), do: false

  def slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: date, start_time: start_time}, now) do
    case Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) do
      :gt -> true
      :lt -> false
      :eq -> Time.compare(start_time, DateTime.to_time(now)) == :gt
    end
  end

  defp validate_slot_in_future(changeset, now) do
    date = get_field(changeset, :scheduled_date)
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)

    cond do
      is_nil(date) or is_nil(start_time) ->
        changeset

      slot_in_future?(%__MODULE__{scheduled_date: date, start_time: start_time}, now) ->
        changeset

      Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) == :lt ->
        add_error(changeset, :scheduled_date, "must be today or later")

      true ->
        add_error(changeset, :start_time, "must be later than the current time")
    end
  end

  # A hidden fallback input keeps `quote[add_ons][]` present in the
  # form even with every add-on unchecked (so unchecking the last one
  # actually clears it) at the cost of always submitting one blank
  # entry alongside any real ones — dropped here rather than left for
  # every caller to filter.
  defp normalize_add_ons(%{"add_ons" => list} = attrs) when is_list(list),
    do: %{attrs | "add_ons" => Enum.reject(list, &(&1 in [nil, ""]))}

  defp normalize_add_ons(attrs), do: attrs
end

    date = get_field(changeset, :scheduled_date)
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)

        changeset

        changeset

      Date.compare(date, DateTime.to_date(now)) == :lt ->
        add_error(changeset, :scheduled_date, "must be today or later")

      true ->

    end

  # form even with every add-on unchecked (so unchecking the last one
  # actually clears it) at the cost of always submitting one blank
  # entry alongside any real ones — dropped here rather than left for
  # every caller to filter.
  defp normalize_add_ons(%{"add_ons" => list} = attrs) when is_list(list),

defmodule CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard do
  @moduledoc """
  The account's configurable rates, one per pricing model.

  A single row per account (see `CleanerCrm.Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card/1`).
  A rate left blank means that pricing model isn't priced yet — quoting
  against it is refused until the owner sets a rate (see
  `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`).

  `weekly_discount_percent`/`biweekly_discount_percent`/`monthly_discount_percent`
  and `add_on_rates_cents` exist for the public instant-quote calculator
  (story 848, see `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing`) — a recurring frequency's
  discount off the one-time subtotal, and the configured price for each
  named add-on (e.g. `"inside_fridge" => 1500`). Unset (`nil`) means no
  discount; an add-on key missing from the map means it isn't priced
  yet, same "never guess a price" rule as the base rates.

  `minimum_visit_cents` is a floor `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing.summarize/2`
  clamps a lead's computed total up to when it's set (e.g. a 1-sqft
  per-sqft quote pricing out at $0.12) — `nil` means no floor.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          per_room_bathroom_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          per_sqft_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          weekly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          biweekly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          monthly_discount_percent: integer() | nil,
          add_on_rates_cents: %{optional(String.t()) => integer()},
          minimum_visit_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "rate_cards" do
    field :per_room_bedroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_room_bathroom_rate_cents, :integer
    field :per_sqft_rate_cents, :integer
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :weekly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :biweekly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :monthly_discount_percent, :integer
    field :add_on_rates_cents, :map, default: %{}
    field :minimum_visit_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @rate_fields ~w(per_room_bedroom_rate_cents per_room_bathroom_rate_cents
                  per_sqft_rate_cents hourly_rate_cents weekly_discount_percent
                  biweekly_discount_percent monthly_discount_percent add_on_rates_cents
                  minimum_visit_cents)a

  @discount_fields ~w(weekly_discount_percent biweekly_discount_percent monthly_discount_percent)a

  def changeset(rate_card, attrs) do
    rate_card
    |> cast(attrs, @rate_fields)
    |> validate_number(:per_room_bedroom_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:per_room_bathroom_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:per_sqft_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_number(:hourly_rate_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> validate_discount_percents()
    |> validate_add_on_rates()
  end

  defp validate_discount_percents(changeset) do
    Enum.reduce(@discount_fields, changeset, fn field, changeset ->
      changeset
      |> validate_number(field, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
      |> validate_number(field, less_than_or_equal_to: 100)
    end)
  end

  # Every configured amount must be a non-negative integer number of
  # cents — the same shape every other rate on this card takes.
  defp validate_add_on_rates(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :add_on_rates_cents) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      rates ->
        if Enum.all?(rates, fn {key, cents} -> is_binary(key) and valid_cents?(cents) end) do
          changeset
        else
          add_error(changeset, :add_on_rates_cents, "must map add-on names to whole cent amounts")
        end
    end
  end

  defp valid_cents?(cents), do: is_integer(cents) and cents >= 0
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing do
  @moduledoc """
  Prices a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead` from the account's rate card:
  the base per-room/per-sqft/hourly amount (reusing
  `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing`, the same math the office quote builder
  uses), each selected add-on's configured amount, and the selected
  frequency's recurring discount off that subtotal.

  Pure and side-effect free, exactly like `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing` —
  `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` calls `summarize/2` on every
  keystroke for the live total.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.{Quote, RateCard}
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing, as: QuotingPricing

  @type line_item :: QuotingPricing.line_item()

  @type summary :: %{
          line_items: [line_item()],
          add_on_items: [line_item()],
          subtotal_cents: integer(),
          discount_percent: integer(),
          total_cents: integer(),
          priceable?: boolean()
        }

  @doc """
  Every number `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` needs to render the
  live total in one call.
  """
  @spec summarize(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: summary()
  def summarize(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead) do
    line_items = base_line_items(rate_card, lead)
    add_on_items = add_on_line_items(rate_card, lead)

    subtotal_cents =
      QuotingPricing.total_cents(line_items) + QuotingPricing.total_cents(add_on_items)

    discount_percent = discount_percent(rate_card, lead)

    %{
      line_items: line_items,
      add_on_items: add_on_items,
      subtotal_cents: subtotal_cents,
      discount_percent: discount_percent,
      total_cents: apply_discount(subtotal_cents, discount_percent),
      priceable?: priceable_from_items?(line_items, add_on_items)
    }
  end

  @doc "The base (room/sqft/hourly) line items, priced the same way an office quote is."
  @spec base_line_items(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: [line_item()]
  def base_line_items(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead) do
    QuotingPricing.line_items(rate_card, %Quote{
      pricing_model: lead.pricing_model,
      bedroom_count: lead.bedroom_count,
      bathroom_count: lead.bathroom_count,
      square_feet: lead.square_feet,
      hours: lead.hours
    })
  end

  @doc """
  One line item per selected add-on, `rate_cents: nil` when the rate
  card hasn't configured a price for it yet — the same "never guess"
  rule `CleanerCrm.Quoting.Pricing.missing_rate?/1` applies to the base
  rates.
  """
  @spec add_on_line_items(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: [line_item()]
  def add_on_line_items(%RateCard{add_on_rates_cents: rates}, %Lead{add_ons: add_ons}) do
    Enum.map(add_ons, fn key ->
      rate_cents = Map.get(rates || %{}, key)

      %{
        description: humanize(key),
        quantity: 1,
        rate_cents: rate_cents,
        amount_cents: rate_cents || 0
      }
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Whether this lead is priceable at all: at least one priced base line
  item, and no selected item (base or add-on) missing a rate.
  """
  @spec priceable?(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: boolean()
  def priceable?(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{} = lead) do
    priceable_from_items?(base_line_items(rate_card, lead), add_on_line_items(rate_card, lead))
  end

  defp priceable_from_items?(line_items, add_on_items) do
    line_items != [] and
      not QuotingPricing.missing_rate?(line_items) and
      not QuotingPricing.missing_rate?(add_on_items)
  end

  @doc "The discount percent (0 when unset) the rate card configures for a lead's frequency."
  @spec discount_percent(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: integer()
  def discount_percent(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{frequency: frequency}) do
    case frequency do
      :weekly -> rate_card.weekly_discount_percent || 0
      :biweekly -> rate_card.biweekly_discount_percent || 0
      :monthly -> rate_card.monthly_discount_percent || 0
      _one_time_or_nil -> 0
    end
  end

  defp apply_discount(subtotal_cents, 0), do: subtotal_cents

  defp apply_discount(subtotal_cents, discount_percent) do
    subtotal_cents
    |> Decimal.new()
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.new(100 - discount_percent))
    |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end

  defp humanize(key) do
    key
    |> String.replace("_", " ")
    |> String.capitalize()
  end
end

      not QuotingPricing.missing_rate?(line_items) and
      not QuotingPricing.missing_rate?(add_on_items)
  end

  @doc "The discount percent (0 when unset) the rate card configures for a lead's frequency."
  @spec discount_percent(RateCard.t(), Lead.t()) :: integer()
  def discount_percent(%RateCard{} = rate_card, %Lead{frequency: frequency}) do
    case frequency do
      :weekly -> rate_card.weekly_discount_percent || 0
      :biweekly -> rate_card.biweekly_discount_percent || 0
      :monthly -> rate_card.monthly_discount_percent || 0
      _one_time_or_nil -> 0
    end
  end

  defp apply_discount(subtotal_cents, 0), do: subtotal_cents

  defp apply_discount(subtotal_cents, discount_percent) do
    subtotal_cents
    |> Decimal.new()
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.new(100 - discount_percent))
    |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end

  defp humanize(key) do
    key
    |> String.replace("_", " ")
    |> String.capitalize()
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.SettingsLive.BookingPolicy do @moduledoc """ Owner-only editor for the account's `CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy` (story 851 follow-up, issue db25b304): the notice-window hours, the late and same-day cancellation fees, and the policy text shown to a client at booking and in their portal. Before this page existed, the only way to set any of it was a direct database edit. Fees are entered in dollars and converted to cents before they ever reach the changeset — `CancellationPolicy` itself only stores integer cents — mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.RateCard`'s own rate inputs. An account with no saved policy yet edits the same fresh, unsaved, all-zero-fee default that `CleanerCrm.Portal.get_cancellation_policy/1` hands the portal itself — the portal keeps working with those defaults whether or not this page has ever been visited. ## Route * `/app/settings/booking` (`:edit`) — office-only, gated the same as every other office surface (`CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`). ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Portal` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Portal alias CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Cancellation Policy <:subtitle> Notice window and fees enforced on self-service reschedule/cancel in the client portal <.form for={@form} id="cancellation-policy-form" data-test="cancellation-policy-form" phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" >
<.input field={@form[:notice_window_hours]} type="number" min="0" label="Notice window (hours)" data-test="notice-window-input" />

How much notice a client must give to cancel or reschedule free of the late fee.

<.input type="number" step="0.01" min="0" name="policy[late_fee]" id={@form[:late_fee_cents].id} label="Late cancellation fee ($)" value={@fee_inputs.late_fee} errors={field_errors(@form[:late_fee_cents])} data-test="late-fee-input" /> <.input type="number" step="0.01" min="0" name="policy[same_day_fee]" id={@form[:same_day_fee_cents].id} label="Same-day cancellation fee ($)" value={@fee_inputs.same_day_fee} errors={field_errors(@form[:same_day_fee_cents])} data-test="same-day-fee-input" />

Charged instead of the late fee when a visit is cancelled the same day it's scheduled.

<.input field={@form[:policy_text]} type="textarea" label="Policy text shown to clients" data-test="policy-text-input" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving..." variant="primary" data-test="save-cancellation-policy-button" > Save Policy
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope policy = Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id) {:ok, socket |> assign(:page_title, "Cancellation Policy") |> assign(:policy, policy) |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs(policy)) |> assign(:form, to_form(Portal.change_cancellation_policy(scope, policy), as: :policy))} end @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"policy" => params}, socket) do {:noreply, apply_params(socket, params, :validate)} end def handle_event("save", %{"policy" => params}, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope {attrs, fee_inputs} = build_attrs(params) case Portal.set_cancellation_policy(scope, attrs) do {:ok, updated} -> {:noreply, socket |> put_flash(:info, "Cancellation policy updated.") |> assign(:policy, updated) |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs(updated)) |> assign(:form, to_form(Portal.change_cancellation_policy(scope, updated), as: :policy))} {:error, changeset} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :policy))} end end defp apply_params(socket, params, action) do {attrs, fee_inputs} = build_attrs(params) changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Portal.change_cancellation_policy(socket.assigns.policy, attrs) |> Map.put(:action, action) socket |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :policy)) end # Builds the changeset attrs (dollar inputs converted to cents) # alongside the raw dollar strings to redisplay — the same pair # both `validate` and `save` need, so both event handlers go through # here, mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.RateCard#build_attrs/2`. defp build_attrs(params) do fee_inputs = %{ late_fee: Map.get(params, "late_fee", ""), same_day_fee: Map.get(params, "same_day_fee", "") } attrs = %{ "notice_window_hours" => Map.get(params, "notice_window_hours"), "late_fee_cents" => dollars_to_cents(fee_inputs.late_fee), "same_day_fee_cents" => dollars_to_cents(fee_inputs.same_day_fee), "policy_text" => Map.get(params, "policy_text") } {attrs, fee_inputs} end defp fee_inputs(%CancellationPolicy{} = policy) do %{ late_fee: cents_to_dollars(policy.late_fee_cents), same_day_fee: cents_to_dollars(policy.same_day_fee_cents) } end defp cents_to_dollars(nil), do: "" defp cents_to_dollars(cents), do: cents |> Decimal.new() |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100)) |> Decimal.to_string(:normal) # An unparseable dollar amount (or a blank input) becomes `nil` # rather than raising, left for `CancellationPolicy.changeset/2`'s # own `validate_required`/`validate_number` to reject. defp dollars_to_cents(dollars) when is_binary(dollars) do case Decimal.parse(String.trim(dollars)) do {decimal, ""} -> decimal |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer() _ -> nil end end defp dollars_to_cents(_dollars), do: nil defp field_errors(field) do if Phoenix.Component.used_input?(field), do: Enum.map(field.errors, &translate_error/1), else: [] end end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.SettingsLive.BookingPolicy do @moduledoc """ Owner-only editor for the account's `CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy` (story 851 follow-up, issue db25b304): the notice-window hours, the late and same-day cancellation fees, and the policy text shown to a client at booking and in their portal. Before this page existed, the only way to set any of it was a direct database edit. Fees are entered in dollars and converted to cents before they ever reach the changeset — `CancellationPolicy` itself only stores integer cents — mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.RateCard`'s own rate inputs. An account with no saved policy yet edits the same fresh, unsaved, all-zero-fee default that `CleanerCrm.Portal.get_cancellation_policy/1` hands the portal itself — the portal keeps working with those defaults whether or not this page has ever been visited. Also hosts the public booking storefront toggle (`CleanerCrm.Accounts.set_storefront/2`) — the account `CleanerCrm.Booking.public_scope/0` prices `/book` against. Unlike the cancellation policy above, this is owner-only (see `CleanerCrm.Authorization`): flipping it can silently steal the public storefront from another account, so an admin viewing this page sees its current value but can't change it. ## Route * `/app/settings/booking` (`:edit`) — office-only, gated the same as every other office surface (`CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`). ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Accounts` - `CleanerCrm.Portal` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Accounts alias CleanerCrm.Portal alias CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header> Cancellation Policy <:subtitle> Notice window and fees enforced on self-service reschedule/cancel in the client portal <.form for={@form} id="cancellation-policy-form" data-test="cancellation-policy-form" phx-change="validate" phx-submit="save" >
<.input field={@form[:notice_window_hours]} type="number" min="0" label="Notice window (hours)" data-test="notice-window-input" />

How much notice a client must give to cancel or reschedule free of the late fee.

<.input type="number" step="0.01" min="0" name="policy[late_fee]" id={@form[:late_fee_cents].id} label="Late cancellation fee ($)" value={@fee_inputs.late_fee} errors={field_errors(@form[:late_fee_cents])} data-test="late-fee-input" /> <.input type="number" step="0.01" min="0" name="policy[same_day_fee]" id={@form[:same_day_fee_cents].id} label="Same-day cancellation fee ($)" value={@fee_inputs.same_day_fee} errors={field_errors(@form[:same_day_fee_cents])} data-test="same-day-fee-input" />

Charged instead of the late fee when a visit is cancelled the same day it's scheduled.

<.input field={@form[:policy_text]} type="textarea" label="Policy text shown to clients" data-test="policy-text-input" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Saving..." variant="primary" data-test="save-cancellation-policy-button" > Save Policy
""" end @impl true def mount(_params, _session, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope policy = Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id) {:ok, socket |> assign(:page_title, "Cancellation Policy") |> assign(:policy, policy) |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs(policy)) |> assign(:form, to_form(Portal.change_cancellation_policy(scope, policy), as: :policy))} end @impl true def handle_event("validate", %{"policy" => params}, socket) do {:noreply, apply_params(socket, params, :validate)} end def handle_event("save", %{"policy" => params}, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope {attrs, fee_inputs} = build_attrs(params) case Portal.set_cancellation_policy(scope, attrs) do {:ok, updated} -> {:noreply, socket |> put_flash(:info, "Cancellation policy updated.") |> assign(:policy, updated) |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs(updated)) |> assign(:form, to_form(Portal.change_cancellation_policy(scope, updated), as: :policy))} {:error, changeset} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :policy))} end end defp apply_params(socket, params, action) do {attrs, fee_inputs} = build_attrs(params) changeset = socket.assigns.current_scope |> Portal.change_cancellation_policy(socket.assigns.policy, attrs) |> Map.put(:action, action) socket |> assign(:fee_inputs, fee_inputs) |> assign(:form, to_form(changeset, as: :policy)) end # Builds the changeset attrs (dollar inputs converted to cents) # alongside the raw dollar strings to redisplay — the same pair # both `validate` and `save` need, so both event handlers go through # here, mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.RateCard#build_attrs/2`. defp build_attrs(params) do fee_inputs = %{ late_fee: Map.get(params, "late_fee", ""), same_day_fee: Map.get(params, "same_day_fee", "") } attrs = %{ "notice_window_hours" => Map.get(params, "notice_window_hours"), "late_fee_cents" => dollars_to_cents(fee_inputs.late_fee), "same_day_fee_cents" => dollars_to_cents(fee_inputs.same_day_fee), "policy_text" => Map.get(params, "policy_text") } {attrs, fee_inputs} end defp fee_inputs(%CancellationPolicy{} = policy) do %{ late_fee: cents_to_dollars(policy.late_fee_cents), same_day_fee: cents_to_dollars(policy.same_day_fee_cents) } end defp cents_to_dollars(nil), do: "" defp cents_to_dollars(cents), do: cents |> Decimal.new() |> Decimal.div(Decimal.new(100)) |> Decimal.to_string(:normal) # An unparseable dollar amount (or a blank input) becomes `nil` # rather than raising, left for `CancellationPolicy.changeset/2`'s # own `validate_required`/`validate_number` to reject. defp dollars_to_cents(dollars) when is_binary(dollars) do case Decimal.parse(String.trim(dollars)) do {decimal, ""} -> decimal |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer() _ -> nil end end defp dollars_to_cents(_dollars), do: nil defp field_errors(field) do if Phoenix.Component.used_input?(field), do: Enum.map(field.errors, &translate_error/1), else: [] end end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.AcceptTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 4e985412: the `/book/accept/:token` slot-selection form
  accepted any date, including years in the past, with zero
  validation — QA drove `scheduled_date=2020-01-01` through card
  capture and it converted into a real scheduled job. No spex/BDD
  story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead. See also
  `CleanerCrm.BookingTest` for the context-level (`Booking`/`Lead`)
  coverage, including the defense-in-depth re-check at confirmation.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      Booking.create_lead(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  test "a past scheduled date is rejected with a clear error and never reaches the confirm step",
       %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    lead = lead_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

    html =
      accept_live
      |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
        booking: %{scheduled_date: "2020-01-01", start_time: "09:00"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

    assert html =~ "must be today or later"
    assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='slot-form']")
    refute has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='confirmation-form']")

    reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
    assert reloaded.scheduled_date == nil
  end

  test "a valid future date advances to the confirmation step", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    lead = lead_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, accept_live, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book/accept/#{lead.acceptance_token}")

    accept_live
    |> form("[data-test='slot-form']",
      booking: %{
        scheduled_date: Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
        start_time: "09:00"
      }
    )
    |> render_submit()

    assert has_element?(accept_live, "[data-test='confirmation-form']")
  end
end
