defmodule CleanerCrm.BookingTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 4e985412: `/book/accept/:token`'s slot-selection form
  accepted any date — including years in the past — with zero
  validation, and QA drove a `scheduled_date` of 2020-01-01 all the
  way through card capture into a real scheduled job. Both guards
  added for it are exercised here:

    * `Lead.slot_changeset/3` (via `Booking.select_slot/3`) — the
      form-level guard, rejecting a past date/time outright.
    * `Booking.confirm_booking/3` — the defense-in-depth re-check
      right before a card is charged, in case a slot that was future
      at selection time goes stale (or a lead's slot fields were set
      some other way) by the time the client actually submits payment.

  No spex/BDD story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead,
  mirroring `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.TemplatesTest`'s precedent for
  issue-only coverage.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.DataCase, async: true

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp lead_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, lead} =
      Booking.create_lead(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          pricing_model: :per_room,
          bedroom_count: 3,
          bathroom_count: 2,
          frequency: :one_time,
          total_cents: 19_500,
          status: :accepted,
          client_name: "Dana Prescott",
          client_email: "dana-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
          client_phone: "+15555550100"
        })
      )

    lead
  end

  describe "select_slot/3" do
    test "rejects a scheduled_date years in the past" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => "2020-01-01",
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert "must be today or later" in errors_on(changeset).scheduled_date
    end

    test "rejects today's date once the chosen start time has already passed" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      today = Date.utc_today()
      now = DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")

      assert {:error, changeset} =
               Booking.select_slot(
                 lead,
                 %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
                 now
               )

      assert "must be later than the current time" in errors_on(changeset).start_time
    end

    test "accepts a future date" do
      lead = lead_fixture(scope_fixture())
      future_date = Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)

      assert {:ok, slotted} =
               Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
                 "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(future_date),
                 "start_time" => "09:00"
               })

      assert slotted.scheduled_date == future_date
    end
  end

  describe "confirm_booking/3 (defense in depth against a past slot)" do
    test "refuses a lead whose slot fields are already in the past, without charging a card" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      past_lead = %{lead | scheduled_date: ~D[2020-01-01], start_time: ~T[09:00:00]}

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(past_lead, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      reloaded = Booking.get_lead_by_token(lead.acceptance_token)
      assert reloaded.status == :accepted
      assert reloaded.stripe_payment_intent_id == nil
    end

    test "refuses a slot picked for later today once that time has passed by confirmation" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)
      today = Date.utc_today()

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(
          lead,
          %{"scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(today), "start_time" => "14:00"},
          DateTime.new!(today, ~T[13:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
        )

      assert {:error, :slot_in_past} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(
                 slotted,
                 %{"policy_agreed" => "true", "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"},
                 DateTime.new!(today, ~T[15:00:00], "Etc/UTC")
               )
    end

    test "still confirms and moves the lead to payment_pending for a genuinely future slot" do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      lead = lead_fixture(scope)

      {:ok, slotted} =
        Booking.select_slot(lead, %{
          "scheduled_date" => Date.to_iso8601(Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 10)),
          "start_time" => "09:00"
        })

      assert {:ok, updated} =
               Booking.confirm_booking(slotted, %{
                 "policy_agreed" => "true",
                 "payment_method" => "pm_card_visa"
               })

      assert updated.status == :payment_pending
    end
  end
end

  missing `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (any dev machine,

      Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, original)
    end)

    Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])
    :ok
  end

  describe "create_payment_intent/1 with no STRIPE_SECRET_KEY configured" do

      assert {:error, %{"code" => "not_configured"}} =
               Live.create_payment_intent(%{amount_cents: 15_000, payment_method: "pm_card_visa"})
    end
  end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking.LeadTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Unit coverage for `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead`'s own changesets: input
  bounds on the calculator's quote fields (issue: any integer was
  accepted with zero validation — a 1-sqft or 40-bedroom quote both
  went through) and `client_email` format on the full acceptance
  changeset (format-only; a click-a-link verification is a separate,
  not-yet-made product decision).
  """

  use ExUnit.Case, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead

  describe "quote_changeset/2 room-count bounds" do
    test "accepts bedroom/bathroom counts at the edges of 0..20" do
      changeset = Lead.quote_changeset(%Lead{}, %{bedroom_count: 0, bathroom_count: 20})

      refute changeset.errors[:bedroom_count]
      refute changeset.errors[:bathroom_count]
    end

    test "rejects a bedroom count above 20" do
      changeset = Lead.quote_changeset(%Lead{}, %{bedroom_count: 21})

      assert {_message, _opts} = changeset.errors[:bedroom_count]
    end

    test "rejects a bathroom count above 20" do
      changeset = Lead.quote_changeset(%Lead{}, %{bathroom_count: 21})

      assert {_message, _opts} = changeset.errors[:bathroom_count]
    end
  end

  describe "quote_changeset/2 square footage bounds" do
    test "accepts square footage within 200..20,000" do
      changeset = Lead.quote_changeset(%Lead{}, %{square_feet: 2000})

      refute changeset.errors[:square_feet]
    end

    test "rejects a 1-sqft quote with a friendly message" do
      changeset = Lead.quote_changeset(%Lead{}, %{square_feet: 1})

      assert {"must be between 200 and 20,000 sq ft", _opts} = changeset.errors[:square_feet]
    end

    test "rejects square footage above 20,000 with the same friendly message" do
      changeset = Lead.quote_changeset(%Lead{}, %{square_feet: 20_001})

      assert {"must be between 200 and 20,000 sq ft", _opts} = changeset.errors[:square_feet]
    end
  end

  describe "quote_changeset/2 hours bounds" do
    test "accepts hours within 1..12" do
      changeset = Lead.quote_changeset(%Lead{}, %{hours: 1})

      refute changeset.errors[:hours]
    end

    test "rejects zero hours with a friendly message" do
      changeset = Lead.quote_changeset(%Lead{}, %{hours: 0})

      assert {"must be between 1 and 12 hours", _opts} = changeset.errors[:hours]

defmodule CleanerCrm.Booking.PricingTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Unit coverage for `CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing.summarize/2`'s minimum
  visit price floor (the rate card's `minimum_visit_cents`) — kills the
  "1-sqft, $0.12 quote" abuse class outright, independent of (and ahead
  of) `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead`'s own input bounds.
  """

  use ExUnit.Case, async: true

  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead
  alias CleanerCrm.Booking.Pricing
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard

  describe "summarize/2 minimum visit price" do
    test "leaves the total untouched and the flag false when no minimum is configured" do
      rate_card = %RateCard{per_sqft_rate_cents: 12, minimum_visit_cents: nil}
      lead = %Lead{pricing_model: :per_sqft, square_feet: 200, add_ons: []}

      summary = Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)

      assert summary.total_cents == 2_400
      refute summary.minimum_applied?
    end

    test "clamps a below-minimum total up to the configured floor and flags it" do
      rate_card = %RateCard{per_sqft_rate_cents: 12, minimum_visit_cents: 8_900}
      lead = %Lead{pricing_model: :per_sqft, square_feet: 200, add_ons: []}

      summary = Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)

      assert summary.total_cents == 8_900
      assert summary.minimum_applied?
    end

    test "leaves an at-or-above-minimum total untouched" do
      rate_card = %RateCard{per_sqft_rate_cents: 100, minimum_visit_cents: 8_900}
      lead = %Lead{pricing_model: :per_sqft, square_feet: 200, add_ons: []}

      summary = Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)

      assert summary.total_cents == 20_000
      refute summary.minimum_applied?
    end

    test "the floor still applies after a frequency discount pulls the total below it" do
      rate_card = %RateCard{
        per_sqft_rate_cents: 100,
        weekly_discount_percent: 90,
        minimum_visit_cents: 8_900
      }

      lead = %Lead{pricing_model: :per_sqft, square_feet: 200, frequency: :weekly, add_ons: []}

      # Subtotal $200.00, discounted 90% -> $20.00, below the $89 floor.
      summary = Pricing.summarize(rate_card, lead)

      assert summary.total_cents == 8_900
      assert summary.minimum_applied?
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.SettingsLive.BookingPolicyTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue db25b304: no owner UI ever edited
  `CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy` — only a direct database edit
  reached the notice-window hours, late/same-day fees, or policy text
  the client portal enforces and displays.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp log_in(conn, scope), do: log_in_user(conn, scope.user)

  test "renders the account's current policy, defaulting to zero fees when unset", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()

    {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='notice-window-input']")
    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='late-fee-input']")
    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='same-day-fee-input']")
    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='policy-text-input']")
  end

  test "saves notice window, fees, and policy text, converting dollars to cents", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    lv
    |> form("[data-test='cancellation-policy-form']",
      policy: %{
        notice_window_hours: "48",
        late_fee: "25.00",
        same_day_fee: "75.50",
        policy_text: "Cancel 48 hours ahead to avoid a fee."
      }
    )
    |> render_submit()

    policy = Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id)

    assert policy.notice_window_hours == 48
    assert policy.late_fee_cents == 2_500
    assert policy.same_day_fee_cents == 7_550
    assert policy.policy_text == "Cancel 48 hours ahead to avoid a fee."
  end

  test "an existing saved policy is preloaded into the form for editing", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()

    {:ok, _policy} =
      Portal.set_cancellation_policy(scope, %{
        notice_window_hours: 24,
        late_fee_cents: 1_000,
        same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
      })

    {:ok, lv, html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    assert html =~ "value=\"10\""
    assert html =~ "value=\"50\""

    lv
    |> form("[data-test='cancellation-policy-form']",
      policy: %{late_fee: "12.00"}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    assert Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id).late_fee_cents == 1_200
  end

  test "rejects a negative notice window", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    html =
      lv
      |> form("[data-test='cancellation-policy-form']",
        policy: %{notice_window_hours: "-5", late_fee: "10.00", same_day_fee: "20.00"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

    assert html =~ "must be greater than or equal to"
    assert Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id).notice_window_hours == 24
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.SettingsLive.BookingPolicyTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue db25b304: no owner UI ever edited
  `CleanerCrm.Portal.CancellationPolicy` — only a direct database edit
  reached the notice-window hours, late/same-day fees, or policy text
  the client portal enforces and displays.

  Also covers the public booking storefront toggle
  (`CleanerCrm.Accounts.set_storefront/2`) this page hosts — the live
  UAT regression where any new signup's account could silently steal
  the `/book` storefront from an existing one.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Portal
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp log_in(conn, scope), do: log_in_user(conn, scope.user)

  test "renders the account's current policy, defaulting to zero fees when unset", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()

    {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='notice-window-input']")
    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='late-fee-input']")
    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='same-day-fee-input']")
    assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='policy-text-input']")
  end

  test "saves notice window, fees, and policy text, converting dollars to cents", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    lv
    |> form("[data-test='cancellation-policy-form']",
      policy: %{
        notice_window_hours: "48",
        late_fee: "25.00",
        same_day_fee: "75.50",
        policy_text: "Cancel 48 hours ahead to avoid a fee."
      }
    )
    |> render_submit()

    policy = Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id)

    assert policy.notice_window_hours == 48
    assert policy.late_fee_cents == 2_500
    assert policy.same_day_fee_cents == 7_550
    assert policy.policy_text == "Cancel 48 hours ahead to avoid a fee."
  end

  test "an existing saved policy is preloaded into the form for editing", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()

    {:ok, _policy} =
      Portal.set_cancellation_policy(scope, %{
        notice_window_hours: 24,
        late_fee_cents: 1_000,
        same_day_fee_cents: 5_000
      })

    {:ok, lv, html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    assert html =~ "value=\"10\""
    assert html =~ "value=\"50\""

    lv
    |> form("[data-test='cancellation-policy-form']",
      policy: %{late_fee: "12.00"}
    )
    |> render_submit()

    assert Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id).late_fee_cents == 1_200
  end

  test "rejects a negative notice window", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()
    {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

    html =
      lv
      |> form("[data-test='cancellation-policy-form']",
        policy: %{notice_window_hours: "-5", late_fee: "10.00", same_day_fee: "20.00"}
      )
      |> render_submit()

    assert html =~ "must be greater than or equal to"
    assert Portal.get_cancellation_policy(scope.active_account_id).notice_window_hours == 24
  end

  describe "storefront toggle" do
    test "an owner can turn the storefront on, which unsets any other account's flag", %{
      conn: conn
    } do
      owner_scope = scope_fixture()
      other_scope = scope_fixture()
      {:ok, _} = Accounts.set_storefront(other_scope, true)

      {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, owner_scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

      refute has_element?(lv, "[data-test='storefront-active-note']")

      lv |> element("[data-test='storefront-toggle']") |> render_click()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='storefront-active-note']")

      assert Accounts.get_account!(owner_scope, owner_scope.active_account_id).storefront
      refute Accounts.get_account!(other_scope, other_scope.active_account_id).storefront
    end

    test "an owner can turn the storefront back off", %{conn: conn} do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      {:ok, _} = Accounts.set_storefront(scope, true)

      {:ok, lv, _html} = live(log_in(conn, scope), ~p"/app/settings/booking")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='storefront-active-note']")

      lv |> element("[data-test='storefront-toggle']") |> render_click()

      refute has_element?(lv, "[data-test='storefront-active-note']")
      refute Accounts.get_account!(scope, scope.active_account_id).storefront
    end

    test "an admin sees the toggle disabled and cannot flip it", %{conn: conn} do
      owner_scope = scope_fixture()
      admin_user = user_fixture()

      {:ok, _member} =
        Accounts.add_user_to_account(
          owner_scope,
          admin_user.id,
          owner_scope.active_account_id,
          :admin
        )

      {:ok, lv, html} = live(log_in(conn, admin_user), ~p"/app/settings/booking")

      assert html =~ "Only the account owner can change this."

      assert lv
             |> element("[data-test='storefront-toggle']")
             |> render() =~ "disabled"
    end
  end
end

  prices from `CleanerCrm.Quoting.RateCard`'s base rates, frequency
  discounts, and add-on prices, but no owner UI ever set the discount
  or add-on fields (QA had to seed them via psql). No spex/BDD story
  owns this surface (story 835's own spex covers the narrower,
  cents-denominated rate-card form embedded in `QuoteLive.Builder`),
  so it's covered here instead.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp log_in(conn, scope), do: log_in_user(conn, scope.user)

  test "renders the current rate card's base rates, discounts, and add-ons", %{conn: conn} do
    scope = scope_fixture()

    {:ok, _rate_card} =
      Quoting.update_rate_card(scope, Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope), %{
        per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 3500,
        per_sqft_rate_cents: 12,
        hourly_rate_cents: 4000,
        weekly_discount_percent: 10,
        add_on_rates_cents: %{"inside_fridge" => 1500}
      })

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.QuoteTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers the live UAT regression where `/book` resolved the *newest*
  account unconditionally (three UAT accounts named "Desert First
  Cleaning" existed, and the newest — with a blank rate card — silently
  became the public storefront), plus the input-bounds and
  minimum-visit-price fixes that shipped alongside it. Story 848's own
  spex drives the calculator's core pricing behavior; this covers the
  issue-only surfaces it doesn't.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest
  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Quoting
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  defp scope_fixture do
    user = user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    {:ok, account} =
      Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})

    %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
  end

  defp rate_card_fixture(scope, attrs) do
    rate_card = Quoting.get_or_create_rate_card(scope)
    {:ok, rate_card} = Quoting.update_rate_card(scope, rate_card, attrs)
    rate_card
  end

  describe "storefront account resolution" do
    test "renders the unavailable state when no business account exists at all", %{conn: conn} do
      {:ok, _lv, html} = live(conn, ~p"/book")

      assert html =~ "Online quotes are not open yet"
    end

    test "renders the unavailable state when two accounts exist and neither is the storefront",
         %{conn: conn} do
      scope_fixture()
      scope_fixture()

      {:ok, _lv, html} = live(conn, ~p"/book")

      assert html =~ "Online quotes are not open yet"
    end

    test "prices against the storefront-flagged account even though a newer account exists", %{
      conn: conn
    } do
      older = scope_fixture()
      {:ok, _} = Accounts.set_storefront(older, true)
      rate_card_fixture(older, %{per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 5000})

      newer = scope_fixture()
      rate_card_fixture(newer, %{per_room_bedroom_rate_cents: 999_999})

      {:ok, lv, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book")

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='quote-form']", quote: %{pricing_model: "per_room", bedroom_count: 1})
      |> render_change()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$50.00")
    end
  end

  describe "quote input bounds" do
    setup %{conn: conn} do
      scope = scope_fixture()
      rate_card_fixture(scope, %{per_sqft_rate_cents: 12, hourly_rate_cents: 4000})
      {:ok, lv, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book")
      %{lv: lv}
    end

    test "rejects square footage below 200 with a friendly message", %{lv: lv} do
      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']", quote: %{pricing_model: "per_sqft", square_feet: 1})
        |> render_change()

      assert html =~ "must be between 200 and 20,000 sq ft"
      refute has_element?(lv, "[data-test='quote-total']")
    end

    test "rejects more than 12 hours with a friendly message", %{lv: lv} do
      html =
        lv
        |> form("[data-test='quote-form']", quote: %{pricing_model: "hourly", hours: 13})
        |> render_change()

      assert html =~ "must be between 1 and 12 hours"
      refute has_element?(lv, "[data-test='quote-total']")
    end
  end

  describe "minimum visit price" do
    test "clamps a below-minimum quote up to the floor and shows the note", %{conn: conn} do
      scope = scope_fixture()

      rate_card_fixture(scope, %{
        per_sqft_rate_cents: 12,
        minimum_visit_cents: 8_900
      })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book")

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='quote-form']", quote: %{pricing_model: "per_sqft", square_feet: 200})
      |> render_change()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$89.00")
      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='minimum-visit-price-note']")
    end

    test "does not show the note when the total is already above the minimum", %{conn: conn} do
      scope = scope_fixture()

      rate_card_fixture(scope, %{
        per_sqft_rate_cents: 100,
        minimum_visit_cents: 8_900
      })

      {:ok, lv, _html} = live(conn, ~p"/book")

      lv
      |> form("[data-test='quote-form']", quote: %{pricing_model: "per_sqft", square_feet: 1000})
      |> render_change()

      assert has_element?(lv, "[data-test='quote-total']", "$1,000.00")
      refute has_element?(lv, "[data-test='minimum-visit-price-note']")
    end
  end
end

content.text:
I've completed all four booking-funnel fixes and reported back to the team lead. Summary of the work:

**1. Storefront account bug** — Added `accounts.storefront` boolean (migration `20260709200010_add_storefront_to_accounts`, plus a partial unique index as DB-level defense in depth). `Booking.resolve_public_account_id/0` now resolves: the account flagged `storefront=true` → else the only account if exactly one exists → else `nil`. Added `Accounts.set_storefront/2`, owner-gated via a new `:manage_storefront` authorization action, which unsets any other account's flag in the same transaction. The toggle lives on `/app/settings/booking`, visible but disabled for non-owners.

**2. Quote input bounds** — `Lead.quote_changeset/2` now enforces bedroom/bathroom counts 0–20, square footage 200–20,000, and hours 1–12, with friendly messages for the latter two. While testing I found the calculator still displayed a live (wrong) total for out-of-bounds input since `priceable?` only checked quantity > 0, not changeset validity — fixed by gating the total/contact-form display on `changeset.valid?` too.

**3. Minimum visit price** — Added `rate_cards.minimum_visit_cents` (migration `20260709200020_add_minimum_visit_cents_to_rate_cards`), editable in dollars alongside the other rate-card fields. `Booking.Pricing.summarize/2` clamps the total to the floor when set, exposing a `minimum_applied?` flag the calculator renders as "Includes our minimum visit price."

**4. Email format** — `Lead.changeset/2` now validates `client_email` with the same regex/message `Users.User` uses (format-only, no verification).

All verification passed: `mix spex` 143/143, `mix test` 308/308 (baseline was 266+, added ~40 new regression tests), `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean, `mix format` clean. Migrations already applied to the local test DB.

**This needs a release rebuild and migration run in UAT/production** before it takes effect.
